Question: To which of the following sectors of the economy, the activity of agriculture -and services belong to?
Explanation: Solution: Primary activities are directly dependent on environment as these refer to utilisation of Earth’s resources, such as land, water, vegetation, building materials and minerals. It, thus includes, hunting and gathering, pastoral activities, fishing, forestry, agriculture, and mining and quarrying. The workers are called red collared workers. Secondary activities add value to natural resources by transforming raw materials into valuable products. Secondary activities, therefore, are concerned with manufacturing, processing and construction (infrastructure) industries. These jobs are called blue collared workers job. Tertiary activities include both production and exchange. The production involves the ’provision’ of services that are ‘consumed. Exchange involves trade, transport and communication facilities that are used to overcome distance. Tertiary jobs are called White Collar Jobs. Quaternary activities are specialised tertairy activities in the Knowledge Sector’ which demands a separate classification. There has been a very high growth in demand for and consumption of information-based services from mutual fund managers to tax consultants, software developers and statisticians. Quinary activities are services that focus on the creation, rearrangement and interpretation of new and existing ideas; data interpretation and the use and evaluation of new technologies. Question: Statement : I. For early societies, historians retrieve information about elite families mostly from inscriptions. II. Satavahana inscriptions generally end with the term Putra, a Prakrit word meaning ‘son’.
Explanation: Solution: For early societies, historians can retrieve information  about elite families fairly easily. Historians often use textual  traditions to understand these processes . For example, though the central story of Mahabharata is about two sets of warring cousins, the text also contains sections laying down norms of behaviour for various social groups.The historians can  also catch a glimpse of some social actors from inscriptions.It is, however, far more difficult to reconstruct the familial relationships of ordinary people. Question: Statement : I. In 1856. Nawab Wajid Ali Shah was dethroned and exiled to Calcutta on the plea that the region was being misgoverned. II. The Nawab was accused of being unable to control the rebellious chiefs and Taluqdars.
Explanation: Solution: Lord Dalhousie’s annexations created disaffection in all the areas and principalities that were annexed but nowhere more so than in the kingdom of Awadh in the heart of North India. Here, Nawab Wajid Ali Shah was dethroned and exiled to Calcutta on the plea that the region  was being misgoverned. The British government also wrongly assumed that Wajid Ali Shah was an unpopular ruler. He was accused of being unable to control the rebellious chiefs and the Taluqdars. The truth is, by the terms of the Subsidiary Alliance of 1801, that had been imposed on Awadh, the Nawab had to disband his military force,  allow the British to position their troops within the kingdom , and act in accordance with the advice of the British Resident who was attached to the court. Deprived of his armed forces, the Nawab became increasingly dependent on British to maintain law and order within the kingdom. He could no longer assert control over the rebellious chiefs and Taluqdars. © examsnet.com

Finally, the Poona Pact was signed between Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar and Mahatma Gandhi on September 24, 1932. The Pact abandoned separate electorates for the depressed classes. Question: Statement : I. The Permanent Settlement was rarely extended to any region beyond Bengal. II. After 1810, the agricultural prices declined affecting adversely the income of the Bengal Zamindars.
Explanation: Solution: The Permanent was of land revenuewas introduced in Bengal and Bihar in 1793 A.D. After 1810, there was a substantial growth in the income of the Zamindars because of the increasing value of harvest produce. The colonial state could not claim any share of this increased income as the revenue demand was fixed in perpetuity. Consequently, the Permanent Settlement  was rarely extended to any region beyond Bengal. Explanation: Solution: Towards the beginning of the twentieth century a new hybrid architectural style developed which combined the Indian with the European. This was called Indo-Saracenic. “Indo” was shorthand for Hindu and “Saracen” was a term Europeans used to designate Muslim. The inspiration for  this style was medieval buildings in India with their domes, chhatris, jalis, arches. By integrating Indian and European styles in public architecture the British wanted to  prove that they were legitimate rulers of India. The Gateway of India, built in the traditional Gujarati style to welcome King George V and Queen Mary to India in 1911, is the most famous example of this style. © examsnet.com

The Lottery Committee was so named because funds for town improvement were raised through public lotteries. In other words, in the early decades of the nineteenth century raising funds for the city was still thought to be the responsibility of public-minded citizens and not exclusively that of the government. The Lottery Committee commissioned a new map of the city so as to get a comprehensive picture of Calcutta. The threat of epidemics gave a further impetus to town planning in the next few decades. Cholera started spreading from 1817 and in 1896 plague made its appearance. The government  proceeded on the basis of the accepted theory of the time: that there was a direct correlation between living conditions  and the spread of disease. Question: Which one of the following statements relating to the power of the President of India to grant pardon is not correct.

Explanation: Solution: The power of the President to grant remission is within its exclusive domain and it is for this reason that our Constitution makers went on to incorporate the provisions of Article 72 and Article 161 to the Constitution of India. Question: The number of angular and radial nodes for 4d orbital is respectively
Explanation: Solution: There are multiple orbitals within an atom. Each has its own specific energy level and properties. Because each orbital is different, they are assigned specific quantum numbers: 1s, 2s, 2p 3s, 3p,4s, 3d, 4p, 5s, 4d, 5p, 6s, 4f, 5d, 6p, 7s, 5f, 6d, 7p. The numbers, (n=1,2,3, etc.) are called principal quantum numbers and can only be positive numbers. The letters (s,p,d,f) represent  the orbital angular momentum quantum number (–!) and the orbital angular momentum quantum number may be 0 or a positive number, but can never be greater than n-1. Each letter is paired with a specific –! value: ●  s: subshell = 0 ●  p: subshell = 1 ●  d: subshell = 2 ●  f: subshell = 3 There are two types of nodes, angular and radial nodes. Angular nodes are typically flat plane (at fixed angles). The –! quantum number determines the number of angular  nodes in an orbital. Radial nodes are spheres (at fixed radius) that occurs as the principal quantum number increases. The total number of  nodes present in any orbital is equal to n-1 Based on the given information in the question, n=4, –! =2 Thus, there are 2 angular nodes present. The total number of nodes in this orbital is: 4-1 = 3. So, there are 3 total nodes. The quantum number –! determines the number of angular nodes. Since there is 2 angular node, this means that one node is still left that should be radial node. So 4d orbital has 2 angular and 1 radial node © examsnet.com

Question: Which one of the following statements regarding the Directive Principles of state policy is NOT correct ?
Option_A: State shall follow the Directive Principles of State Policy both in the matter of administration as well as in the making of laws
Option_B: The Directive Principles of State Policy embody the object of the state under the republican Constitution
Option_C: The Directive Principles of State Policy have precedence over the Fundamental Rights in case of conflict between the two
Option_D: The Directive Principles of State Policy are not enforceable in the courts
Explanation: Solution: The Fundamental Rights are the rights of the individual citizens guaranteed by the Constitution. The directive principles lay down various tenets   of a welfare state. They are just guidelines that should be followed by the government to establish a welfare state. An important difference between the two is that while the fundamental rights are justiciable and can be enforced by the court, the Directive Principles are non-justiciable and cannot be enforced upon the government. The conflict between the two arises when the State needs to implement a directive principle and it infringes/abridges the fundamental rights of the citizens. While Parliament has often tried to assert the supremacy of the state and DPSPs over Fundamental Rights, the Supreme Court has repeatedly held that Directive Principles  could not override a Fundamental Right, and in case of a conflict between the two, the Fundamental Right would prevail over the Directive Principles. Question: According to simple Keynesian theory, the slope of the aggregate consumption curve against income is :
Explanation: Solution: The consumer goods and services demanded by the households constitute the consumption demand. In this regard, Keynes propounded a law known as the ‘Fundamental Psychological Law of Consumption.’ According to Keynes, consumption  depends on personal disposable income and as income rises,  consumption also rises but not as much as the increases in income. That means a part of the increase in income is saved. In other words, Marginal propensity to Consume (MPC) is always less than one. In Keynes’ consumption function, The relationship between consumption spending and income is  usually explained in an equation form : C = a + bY (a > 0; 0 < b < 1) Here, C and Y represent consumption and income, respectively.  This equation indicates that consumption is a linear function of income since it is the equation of a straight line. In the equation, ‘a’ stands for autonomous consumption. This part of consumption spending is independent of the level of income. Its value is positive in the sense that consumption is always positive, even if income is zero, ‘b’ is-the behavioral  coefficient or the MPC.  This part of consumption is  called ‘induced’ consumption. According to Keynes, MPC is always positive, but less than one. Here ‘b’ is the slope of the consumption function. Question: Which of the following theories form the basis of international trade ? 1. Absolute cost difference 2. Comparative cost difference 3. Opportunity cost Select the correct answer using the code given below: [2014 CDS-II]
Explanation: Solution: All the statements form the bases of international trade. Adam Smith propounded the theory of absolute cost advantage/difference as the basis of foreign trade. Under such circumstances, an exchange of goods will take place only if each of the two countries can produceone commodity at an absolutely lower production cost than theother country. David Ricardo developed the classical theory ofcomparative advantage in 1817. Thus, the opportunity cost measures the ratio of marginal costs of the two commodities. © examsnet.com

Kailasanatha Temple was constructed in 8th century by Rashtrakuta king Krishna I in 756- 773 CE. Shore Temple at Mamallapuram was built by Narasimhavarman II in the 8th century. Explanation: Solution: The deeds of Hamza and the deeds of Babur are not depicted in the Rajput paintings. Rajput paintings depict a number of themes, events of epics like the Ramayana and the Mahabharata, Krishna's life, Ragas and Raginis, beautiful landscapes, and humans. Question: Which one of the Five Year Plans had a high priority to bring inflation under control and to achieve stability in the economic situation ? [2016 CDS-I]
Explanation: Solution: The Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974- 79) had a high priority to bring inflation under control and to achieve stability in the economic situation. It laid stress on employment, checking inflation, poverty alleviation (Garibi Hatao), and justice. It also focussed selfreliance in agricultural production and defence. The hyperinflation led the government to hand over a new function to RBI to stabilise the inflation. A judicious price-wage policy was started to check the menace of inflation on wageearners. It targeted an annual growth rate of 5.5 per cent in the National Income. Four Annual Plans were completed in the Fifth Plan period. The Plan was terminated in 1978 (instead of 1979) when the Janata Party came to power. © examsnet.com

Question: Which of the following statement(s) is / are true with respect to Phillips Curve ? 1. It shows the trade-off between unemployment and inflation 2. The downward sloping curve of Phillips Curve is generally held to be valid only in the short run 3. In the long run, Phillips Curve is usually thought to be horizontal at the non-accelerating inflation rate of unemployment (NAIRU) Select the correct answer using the code given below : [2016 CDS-I]
Explanation: Solution: Statements 1 and 2 are true with respect to the Phillips Curve. The Phillips Curve is an economic concept developed by A.W. Phillips showing that inflation and unemployment have a stable and inverse relationship. The theory  states that with economic growth comes inflation, which, in turn, should lead to more jobs and less  unemployment. The non-accelerating inflation rate of unemployment (NAIRU) – also referred to as the long-run Phillips curve – is the specific level of unemployment that is evident in an economy that does not cause inflation to rise up and it is not horizontal. © examsnet.com

Option_C: creating an ombudsman mechanism for reduction of corruption in public life

Explanation: Solution: The Second Administrative Reforms Commission (ARC) (2005) was concerned with reforms in institutional arrangements for good governance. The Second ARC was constituted on August 31, 2005 as a Commission of Inquiry, under the Chairmanship of Shri Veerappa Moily for preparing a detailed blueprint for revamping the public administrative system. Question: As per the Constitution of India, the Writ of Prohibition relates to an order : 1. issued against judicial and quasi­-judicial authority 2. to prohibit an inferior Court from proceeding in a particular case where it has no jurisdiction to try 3. to restrain a person from holding a public office to which he is not entitled Select the correct answer using the code given below : [2016 CDS-I]
Explanation: Solution: Statements (1) and (2) relate to the orders issued under the Writ of Prohibition as per the Constitution of India. The expression 'prohibition' literally means 'to prohibit'. The Writ of Prohibition is a judicial order issued by the Supreme Court or a High Court to an inferior Court or quasi-judicial body forbidding the latter to continue proceedings therein in excess of its jurisdiction or to usurp a jurisdiction with which it is not legally vested. Thus, the objective of the writ is to compel inferior courts to keep themselves within the limits of their jurisdiction. Writ jurisdiction is enjoyed only by the Supreme Court and High Courts under Articles 32 and 226 of the Constitution, respectively. The Constitution makes provisions for writs for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights enshrined in Part III of the Constitution. © examsnet.com

Question: Which one among the following was not an attribute of Samudragupta described in Prayag Prashasti ? [2016 CDS-I]
Explanation: Solution: Accomplished sculptor was not an attribute of Samudragupta as described in Prayag-Prashasti. Harisena was the court poet of Samudragupta, who mentioned the achievements of Samudragupta in the Prayag-Prashasti inscription (or Allahabad Pillar inscription). The inscription is an eulogy of Samudragupta and mentions about the conquests of Samudragupta and boundaries of the Gupta Empire. As per this inscription, Samudragupta defeated 9 kings in North and 12 kings in South. © examsnet.com

Explanation: Solution: Kamandaka's Nitisara is a contribution to political morality. The Nitisara of Kamandaka, also known as the Kamandakiya-Nitisara, was composed during the period of Gupta Dynasty. It was based on Kautilya's Arthashastra. It is a post-Maurya treatise narrating the elements of polity divided into twenty sargas and thirty-six prakarans. It deals with, inter alia, the art in statecraft, diplomacy and aspects of warfare. © examsnet.com

Question: The Lilavati of Bhaskara is a standard text on: [2016 CDS-I]
Explanation: Solution: The Lilavati of Bhaskara is a standard text on Mathematics. The book is a treatise on Mathematics written in 1150. It is the first volume of Bhaskara's main work, the Siddhanta Shiromani, alongside the Bijaganita, the Grahaganita and the Goladhyaya. The book was written for his daughter named Lilavati. A Persian translation of the Lilavati was commissioned in 1587 by Emperor Akbar and it was executed by Faizi. © examsnet.com

Question: Which of the following statement(s) are true with respect to the concept of ‘EFFICIENCY’ as used in mainstream economics ? 1. Efficiency occurs when no possible reorganisation of production can make anyone better off without making someone else worse off 2. An economy is clearly inefficient if it is inside the Production Possibility Frontier (PPF) 3. At a minimum, an efficient economy is on its Production Possibility Frontier (PPF) 4. The terms such as ‘Pareto Efficiency’, ‘Pareto Optimality’ and ‘Allocative Efficiency’ are all essentially one and the same which denote ‘efficiency in resource allocation’ Select the correct answer using the code given below : [2016 CDS-I]
Explanation: Solution: All the statements are true with respect to the concept of 'EFFICIENCY' as used in the mainstream economics. Economic efficiency implies an economic state in which every resource is optimally allocated to serve each individual or entity in the best way while minimising waste and inefficiency. Efficiency occurs when no possible reorganisation of production can make anyone better off without making someone else worse off. An economy is clearly inefficient if it is inside the Production Possibility Frontier (PPF). At a minimum, an efficient economy is on its Production Possibility Frontier (PPF). © examsnet.com

Question: Which one of the following nations has faced severe economic crisis in the year 2015 resulting in default in repayment of IMF loan? [2016 CDS-I]
Explanation: Solution: Greece has faced severe economic crisis in the year 2015 resulting in default in repayment of IMF loan. Greece defaulted on a USD 1.7 billion IMF payment, making it the first developed country to ever default on an IMF loan and the first country to default since Zimbabwe in 2001. The Greek financial crisis was a series of debt crises that began with the global financial crisis of 2008. Its source originated in the mismanagement of the Greek economy and of the government finances, however, rather than exogenous international factors. To compound the problems, Greece's membership in the Eurozone prevented it from exercising full control over its monetary policy. So, interest rates were kept too low for too long relative to the inflationary pressures that were building up in the Greek economy. © examsnet.com

Question: Who among the following Prime Ministers of India were defeated oy a vote of No Confidence ? 1. Morarji Desai 2. Viswanath Pratap Singh 3. H.D. Deve Gowda 4. Atal Bihari Vajpayee Select the correct answer using the code given below : [2016 CDS-I]
Explanation: Solution: Vishwanath Pratap Singh (1990), H.D. Deve Gowda (1997) and Atal Bihari Vajpayee (1999) were the Prime Ministers of India who were defeated by the vote of 'No Confidence'. Morarji Desai had resigned before he faced the motion of 'No Confidence'. In India, a motion of 'No Confidence' can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha (the lower house of the Parliament). If a majority of the members of the House vote in favour of the motion, the motion is passed and the Government is bound to vacate the office. © examsnet.com

Question: Which of the following statements regarding Rajya Sabha is / are correct ? 1. The maximum permissible strength of Rajya Sabha is 250 2. In Rajya Sabha, 238 members are elected indirectly from the States and Union Territories 3. It shares legislative powers equally with Lok Sabha in matters such as creation of All India Services Select the correct answer using the code given below : [2016 CDS-I]
Explanation: Solution: Article 80 of the Constitution lays down the maximum strength of Rajya Sabha as 250, out of which 12 members are nominated by the President and 238 are representatives of the States and of the two Union Territories, who are indirectly elected. If the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting declaring that it is necessary or expedient in the national interest to create one or more All India Services common to the Union and the States, the Parliament becomes empowered to create by law such services (Article 312 of the Constitution).So, statement (3) is incorrect as the power is not available to the Lok Sabha. © examsnet.com

Explanation: Solution: Statements (1) and (4) relating to the office of the President of India are correct. Explanation: Solution: The followers of Gorakhnath were called Nath-Panthis. Gorakhnath was an influential founder of the Nath Hindu monastic movement in India. He is considered as one of the two notable disciples of Matsyendranath. His followers are found in India's Himalayan states, the western and central states and the Gangetic plains as well as in Nepal. Question: What is the maximum number of states of matter? [2017 CDS-I]
Explanation: Solution: The maximum number of states of matter is five. There are five known phases, or states, of matter: solids, liquids, gases, plasma and Bose-Einstein condensates. The main difference in the structures of each state is in the densities of the particles. Plasma is not a common state of matter here on Earth, but may be the most common state of matter in the universe. Plasma consists of highly charged particles with extremely high kinetic energy.The noble gases (helium, neon, argon, krypton, xenon and radon) are often used to make glowing signs by using electricity to ionise them to the plasma state. Stars are essentially super-heated balls of plasma. In 1995, technology enabled the scientists to create a ew state of matter, the BoseEinstein condensate (BEC). Using a combination of lasers and magnets, Eric Cornell and Carl Weiman cooled a sample of rubidium to within a few degrees of absolute zero. At this extremely low temperature, molecular motion comes very close to stopping altogether. Light appears to slow down as it passes through a BEC, allowing study of the particle/wave paradox. A BEC also has many of the properties of a superfluid – flowing without friction. BECs are also used to simulate conditions that might apply in black holes. © examsnet.com

Explanation: Solution: Statements (1) and (2) are correct regarding Article 21. This controlled energy is used in electricity generation and radioactive isotopes production. All the operating nuclear reactors are ‘critical’. Explanation: Solution: James Prinsep deciphered the Brahmi and Kharoshthi scripts. James Prinsep was an English scholar, orientalist and antiquary. He was the founding editor of the Journal of the Asiatic Society of Bengal. The first evidence for the use of Brahmi script in India comes from around 250 B.C. It was used to write several different languages, including Sanskrit and Prakrit. Over 200 modern Indian scripts are based on Brahmi script. Brahmi script is written from left to right and was used to write on a variety of materials such as stone, terracotta and metal. Question: The Deccan Agriculturalists' Relief Act of 1879 was enacted with which one of the following objectives?
Option_A: Restore lands to the dispossessed peasants
Option_B: Ensure financial assistance to peasants during social and religious occasions
Option_C: Restrict the sale of land for indebtedness to outsiders
Option_D: Peasants to be sued where they posses land
Explanation: Solution: Concept: The Deccan Agriculturalists' Relief Act of 1879 aimed to protect peasants from losing their land due to debt to moneylenders. Explanation: The Act was a direct result of the Deccan Riots of 1875. In those riots, peasants attacked moneylenders ( sahukars ) who charged high interest. A commission was set up and reported in 1878. The Act of 1879 introduced two key protections. First, it prevented peasants from being arrested or imprisoned for failing to repay debts. Second, it restricted the sale of land for indebtedness to outsiders (non-agriculturists). This ensured that land remained within the farming community. The Act did not restore lands already lost, nor did it provide financial assistance for ceremonies. It also changed legal procedures so that peasants could only be sued in the district where they owned land. Thus, the core objective was to curb the transfer of agricultural land to moneylenders from outside the village. Answer: Option C: Restrict the sale of land for indebtedness to outsiders. © examsnet.com

Question: The Limitation Law, which was passed by the British in 1859, addressed which one of the following issues?

Option_C: Land bonds could not be executed by moneylenders.
Option_D: Loan bonds would have validity for ten years.
Explanation: Solution: Concept: The Limitation Law of 1859 introduced a time limit for the legal enforceability of loan agreements between moneylenders and peasants (Ryots). Explanation: The Deccan Ryot Commission studied the exploitative lending practices in rural India. It found that moneylenders charged extremely high interest on small principal amounts, often trapping peasants in perpetual debt. To regulate such transactions, the British passed the Limitation Law in 1859. The law required a legally binding bond to be signed between the moneylender and the Ryot. This bond would have legal validity for only three years from the date of signing. After three years, the lender could not sue the borrower to recover the loan. Thus, the law limited the period of enforceability, not the existence of the debt itself. Answer: Loan bonds signed between money-lender and Ryots would have validity only for three years. © examsnet.com

Question: Which one of the following is not an assumption in the law of demand?
Option_A: There are no changes in the taste and preferences of consumers.
Option_C: Consumers are affected by demonstration effect.
Option_D: There are no changes in the price of substitute goods.
Explanation: Solution: Concept: The law of demand assumes all other factors affecting demand remain constant (ceteris paribus). The demonstration effect is a violation of this assumption, not an assumption itself. Explanation: The law of demand states that as price falls, quantity demanded rises, and vice versa, assuming other things remain unchanged. The assumptions include: no change in consumers' taste and preferences, constant income of consumers, no change in the price of substitute goods, no change in population, and no future price expectations. These assumptions isolate the price-quantity relationship. The demonstration effect (or Veblen effect) occurs when consumers buy more of a good because its price is high or because others are buying it. This effect contradicts the inverse relationship of the law of demand. Hence, it is not an assumption; it is an exception to the law. Answer: Option C: Consumers are affected by demonstration effect. © examsnet.com

Question: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct?
Option_A: When total utility is maximum, marginal utility is zero.
Option_B: When total utility is decreasing, marginal utility is negative.
Option_C: When total utility is increasing, marginal utility is positive.
Option_D: When total utility is maximum, marginal, and average utility are equal to each other.
Explanation: Solution: Concept: The relationship between total utility (TU), marginal utility (MU), and average utility (AU) determines the correct statement. Explanation: Total utility (TU) is the sum of marginal utilities (MU) from consuming each unit. When TU is maximum, MU becomes zero because the last unit adds nothing to total satisfaction. When TU is increasing, each additional unit adds positive satisfaction, so MU is positive. When TU is decreasing, the last unit reduces total satisfaction, so MU is negative. Average utility (AU) is TU divided by the number of units consumed. At the point of maximum TU, MU equals zero, but AU is still positive (TU > 0). Thus MU and AU are not equal at maximum TU; AU is greater than MU (which is zero). Therefore, statement D ("When total utility is maximum, marginal and average utility are equal to each other") is incorrect. Answer: Option D. © examsnet.com

Question: Consider the following statements about indifference curves: 1. Indifference curves are convex to the origin. 2. Higher indifference curve represents higher level of satisfaction. 3. Two indifference curves cut each other. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Indifference curves represent combinations of two goods that give a consumer equal satisfaction. Explanation: Statement 1 is correct because indifference curves are convex to the origin. This convexity reflects the diminishing marginal rate of substitution between the two goods. Statement 2 is correct because a higher indifference curve shows a greater quantity of both goods, hence a higher level of satisfaction. Consumers prefer more to less, so moving to a higher curve increases utility. Statement 3 is incorrect because two indifference curves cannot intersect each other. If they intersected, it would imply contradictory levels of satisfaction at the same combination of goods. This violates the transitivity assumption of consumer preferences. Answer: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The correct option is B. © examsnet.com

Question: Which one of the following is not correct about the Panchayats as laid down in Part IX of the Constitution of India?

Option_D: The State Legislature may by law make provisions for audit of accounts of the Panchayats.

Explanation: Option A is correct. However, the option states "whether or not" which is not exactly accurate; but the prevailing interpretation is that the state has the discretion in the manner, including the extent of reservation. Many exam sources consider this statement as correct. Option B is incorrect. Under Article 243C(4), the Chairperson of a Panchayat shall have the right to vote in the meetings of the Panchayat regardless of whether they are chosen by direct election or not. The statement claims that direct election is necessary to exercise voting rights, which is false. Option C is correct. Article 243E states that every Panchayat, unless dissolved sooner, continues for five years from the date of its first meeting. Option D is correct. Question: Which one of the following is not correct about Administrative Tribunals?

These tribunals can try disputes related to recruitment and service conditions of public employees. However, the law establishing such tribunals can exclude the jurisdiction of all courts except the Supreme Court. Specifically, the Supreme Court's power to grant special leave to appeal under Article 136 cannot be taken away. Statement C says tribunals can exclude the jurisdiction of all courts to allow for special leave to appeal – this is misleading. Actually, the exclusion applies to all courts except for the Supreme Court's special leave jurisdiction. Therefore, statement C is incorrect. Question: Which one of the following hypothese postulates that individual's consumption in any time period depends upon resouces available to the individual, rate of return on his capital and age of the individual?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: The Life Cycle Hypothesis, proposed by Ando and Modigliani, states that an individual’s consumption at any time is based on their lifetime resources, expected future income, age, and the return on assets. Explanation: This hypothesis says consumption depends on three main factors. First, the total resources available to the person include current income, wealth, and expected future earnings. Second, the rate of return on capital affects how much the individual can spend today versus save for later. Third, the age of the individual determines the stage of the life cycle – young people borrow, middle-aged save, and old people dissave. These factors together decide the consumption pattern in any given time period. The hypothesis rejects that consumption depends only on current income. Instead, it stresses that people plan their spending over their entire lifetime. This makes the Life Cycle Hypothesis the correct match for the given description. Answer: C. Question: According to John Maynard Keynes, employment depends upon _________.
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Keynes argued that employment is determined by the level of effective demand in the economy. Explanation: Classical economists believed that free markets always ensure full employment through Say's Law and flexible wages. Keynes rejected this, calling full employment a special case, not the general rule. He focused on the demand side of the economy. According to Keynes, the volume of employment depends on the total spending of households, businesses, and the government – i.e., effective demand. Effective demand equals the total expenditure on goods and services at a given price level. If effective demand is low, firms produce less and hire fewer workers, causing unemployment. Only when effective demand is sufficient will full employment be achieved. Keynes explained this in his 1936 book, *The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money*. Answer: C. Effective demand © examsnet.com

Question: Which among the following Arab scientists could be given the credit of christening the mathematical discipline of algorithm?

Explanation: Al‑Khwarizmi (Muhammad ibn Musa al‑Khwarizmi) was a 9th‑century Persian scholar whose work in algebra and arithmetic introduced a logical, step‑wise approach to calculations. His treatise *Al‑Kitab al‑Mukhtasar fi Hisab al‑Jabr wal‑Muqabala* laid the foundation for algebra. The Latin translation of his name, *Algoritmi*, eventually gave rise to the word "algorithm". Question: Which one of the following developments took place because of the Kansas-Nebraska Act of 1854?

This principle is called popular sovereignty. The Act repealed the Missouri Compromise of 1820, which had banned slavery north of latitude 3 6 ∘ 3 0 ′ 36^\circ 30' 3 6 ∘ 3 0 ′ in the Louisiana Purchase territory. As a result, pro-slavery and anti-slavery settlers rushed into Kansas to influence the vote. The first election was marred by fraud and violence, leading to the period known as "Bleeding Kansas." Thus, the main development was the repeal of the Missouri Compromise and the introduction of popular sovereignty. Answer: A. Question: Very small insoluble particles in a liquid may be separated from it by using ________.
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Centrifugation uses high-speed rotation to separate very fine, insoluble solid particles from a liquid based on density differences. Explanation: • Very small insoluble particles settle extremely slowly under normal gravity. • In a centrifuge, the mixture is spun rapidly around an axis. • The resulting centrifugal force pushes denser particles outward to the bottom or walls of the tube. • The clear liquid (supernatant) can then be poured off or removed. • Other techniques fail for such tiny particles: • Crystallization produces pure crystals from a solution, not from a suspension of insoluble solids. • Fractional distillation separates liquids with different boiling points, not solids from a liquid. • Decantation relies on particles settling by gravity; very fine particles remain suspended and do not settle in a reasonable time. • Therefore, centrifugation is the most effective method for separating very small insoluble particles. Answer: C. centrifugation © examsnet.com

Question: Which one of the following elements cannot be detected by "Lassaigne's test"?

Explanation: In Lassaigne's test, the organic compound is fused with sodium metal. This converts covalent elements into ionic forms: sodium cyanide ( N a C N \mathrm{NaCN} NaCN ), sodium sulphide ( N a 2 S \mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{S} Na 2 ​ S ), and sodium halide ( N a X \mathrm{NaX} NaX , where X = C l , B r , I \mathrm{X} = \mathrm{Cl}, \mathrm{Br}, \mathrm{I} X = Cl , Br , I ). For halogens, the sodium halide is then treated with silver nitrate ( A g N O 3 \mathrm{AgNO}_3 AgNO 3 ​ ) to form a precipitate of silver halide ( A g X \mathrm{AgX} AgX ). Fluorine does not form a precipitate under these conditions because silver fluoride ( A g F \mathrm{AgF} AgF ) is soluble in water. Thus, fluorine cannot be detected by Lassaigne's test. Chlorine, bromine, iodine, and sulphur all give characteristic positive tests. Answer: D. F (Fluorine) © examsnet.com

Question: In which of the following, functional group isomerism in not possible?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Functional group isomerism occurs when two or more compounds share the same molecular formula but have different functional groups. Explanation: Alcohols ( R − O H \mathrm{R-OH} R − OH ) and ethers ( R − O − R ′ \mathrm{R-O-R'} R − O − R ′ ) are functional isomers of each other. Aldehydes ( R − C H O \mathrm{R-CHO} R − CHO ) and ketones ( R − C O − R ′ \mathrm{R-CO-R'} R − CO − R ′ ) are functional isomers. Cyanides ( R − C N \mathrm{R-CN} R − CN ) and isocyanides ( R − N C \mathrm{R-NC} R − NC ) are also functional isomers. In alkyl halides (haloalkanes), the halogen atom ( X \mathrm{X} X ) can only form a single bond to carbon. It cannot form multiple bonds or any alternative attachment that would give a different functional group while keeping the same molecular formula. Hence, there is only one possible functional group for any given haloalkane formula. Therefore, functional group isomerism is not possible for alkyl halides. Answer: C. Alkyl halides © examsnet.com

Question: For an ideal gas, which one of the following statements does not hold true?
Option_A: The speed of all gas molecules is same.
Option_B: The kinetic energies of all gas molecules is zero.
Option_C: The potential energy of the gas molecules is zero.
Option_D: There is no interactive force between the molecules.
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Ideal gas model excludes intermolecular forces and potential energy, but molecules have a distribution of speeds and non-zero kinetic energy. Explanation: The kinetic theory assumes molecules are in random motion with different speeds, not all the same. Therefore, statement A ("speed of all molecules is same") is false. Statement B is also false because molecules always possess kinetic energy; zero kinetic energy would imply absolute zero temperature, which is not a property of an ideal gas. Statements C and D are true: for an ideal gas, potential energy is zero and no interactive forces exist between molecules. Thus, both A and B do not hold true for an ideal gas. Question: The Hooke's law is valid for _________.
Option_A: only proportional region of the stress-strain curve
Option_C: entire elastic region of the stress-strain curve
Option_D: elastic as well as plastic region of the stress-strain curve
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Hooke’s law applies only to the initial linear portion of the stress‑strain curve, called the proportional region. Explanation: The law states that stress is directly proportional to strain, i.e., Stress ∝ Strain \text{Stress} \propto \text{Strain} Stress ∝ Strain , so Stress Strain = Young’s modulus (constant) \frac{\text{Stress}}{\text{Strain}} = \text{Young’s modulus (constant)} Strain Stress ​ = Young’s modulus (constant) . This proportionality holds only until the proportional limit, which is within the elastic region but not the whole elastic region. Beyond the proportional limit (even within the elastic limit), the relationship becomes non‑linear and Hooke’s law is no longer valid. Thus, the law is restricted to the proportional region of the stress‑strain curve. Answer: A. only proportional region of the stress‑strain curve © examsnet.com

Question: Which one of the following statements regarding histone proteins is correct?

Option_D: Histones are proteins associated with carbohydrates in the cytosol.
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Histones are basic proteins that help package DNA into structural units inside the nucleus of eukaryotic cells. Explanation: Histones are rich in positively charged amino acids like lysine and arginine. This positive charge allows them to bind tightly to the negatively charged DNA backbone. They organize into octamers, around which DNA wraps to form nucleosomes — the fundamental unit of chromatin. This packaging occurs only in the nucleus, not in mitochondria or the cytosol. Thus, histones are always associated with DNA inside the nucleus. Answer: Option B — Histones are proteins that are present in nucleus in association with DNA. © examsnet.com

Question: Which one of the following statements is correct?

Option_C: Urea is produced from the digestion of starch.
Option_D: Urea is produced in the lungs and the kidneys.
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Urea is a waste product formed in the liver from the breakdown of amino acids. Explanation: The liver processes excess amino acids through deamination. This removes the amino group ( − N H 2 -\mathrm{NH}_2 − NH 2 ​ ), producing ammonia ( N H 3 \mathrm{NH}_3 NH 3 ​ ) and a carbon skeleton. Ammonia is highly toxic, so the liver quickly converts it into urea via the urea cycle. Urea has the formula C O ( N H 2 ) 2 \mathrm{CO}(\mathrm{NH}_2)_2 CO ( NH 2 ​ ) 2 ​ and contains carbon, nitrogen, and oxygen. Once formed, urea enters the bloodstream and is filtered by the kidneys. It is then excreted in urine. Urea is not produced in blood, lungs, kidneys, or from starch digestion. Thus, only option A is correct. Answer: Option A – Urea is produced in the liver. © examsnet.com

Question: Which one of the following river valleys of India is under the influence of intensive gully erosion?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Gully erosion refers to the formation of deep channels (gullies) in soil due to running water, and the Chambal valley is notorious for such erosion, creating bad lands called ravines. Explanation: Running water cuts through clayey soils and forms deep channels called gullies. When soil is removed along definite paths down a slope, it is termed gully erosion. Due to severe gully erosion, the land becomes unfit for cultivation and is called bad land. In the Chambal basin, such bad lands are specifically known as ravines. These ravines occur extensively in the lower course of the Chambal river valley, making it the area most affected by intensive gully erosion in India. Other rivers like Kosi are known for flooding, Damodar for its coal-bearing region, and Brahmaputra for braided channels, but they do not exhibit such extensive gully erosion. Answer: Option B: Chambal © examsnet.com

Question: A car undergoes a uniform circular motion. The acceleration of the car is

Explanation: Solution: Concept: In uniform circular motion, speed is constant but velocity direction changes continuously, so acceleration is always present (centripetal) with constant magnitude but changing direction. Explanation: A car in uniform circular motion moves at constant speed along a circular path. Velocity is a vector; it changes direction every instant even if speed is constant. This change in velocity causes an acceleration called centripetal acceleration. Its magnitude is a = v 2 r a = \frac{v^2}{r} a = r v 2 ​ , which remains constant because v v v and r r r are constant. However, the direction of this acceleration always points toward the centre of the circle. As the car moves, the direction of the centre changes relative to the car, so the acceleration vector rotates continuously. Thus, the acceleration is non‑zero but its direction is not constant — only the magnitude is constant. Therefore, the acceleration is a non‑zero vector that is not constant (i.e., it changes direction). Answer: Option C: a non-zero but not a constant. © examsnet.com

Question: Which one of the following forms of Constitution contains the features of both the Unitary and Federal Constitution?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: A constitution that blends elements of both unitary and federal systems is known as a quasi-federal constitution. Explanation: A federal constitution divides power between a central authority and regional units, with each level enjoying autonomy. A unitary constitution concentrates power in a single central government, with regional units deriving authority from it. A quasi-federal constitution combines both: it is primarily federal in structure but includes unitary features that allow the central government to override or control states when needed. For example, the Indian Constitution has a dual polity (Union and States), a written and rigid constitution, and independent judiciary—these are federal features. At the same time, it includes a single citizenship, an integrated judiciary, All‑India Services, and the power of the Union to legislate on state subjects under certain circumstances—these are unitary features. Therefore, the term “quasi‑federal” correctly describes a constitution that contains characteristics of both unitary and federal systems. Quasi‑unitary would imply that states have unusually broad powers, which is not the case here. Unitary and federal structures, by definition, do not mix features of the other form. Answer: Quasi‑Federal © examsnet.com

Examples include the Mediterranean Basin, California, Central Chile, and South Africa. The region's anti-cyclonic pressure belts create clear skies, aiding fruit development. Question: The concept of "Four Pillar State", free from district magistracy for India was suggested by ________.

Question: Bose-Einstein Condensate is ________.
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Bose-Einstein Condensate (BEC) is a distinct phase of matter that appears at ultra-low temperatures, and it is widely recognized as the fifth state of matter. Explanation: The traditional states of matter are solid, liquid, gas, and plasma. Bose-Einstein Condensate is considered the fifth state because it exhibits entirely different physical properties. It is formed when a dilute gas of bosons is cooled to temperatures extremely close to absolute zero ( 0 K 0\ \text{K} 0 K or − 273.15 ∘ C -273.15\ ^\circ\text{C} − 273.15 ∘ C ). At such low temperatures, the thermal de Broglie wavelength becomes comparable to the interparticle distance. A large fraction of the bosons then collapses into the lowest quantum state (the ground state). All the atoms in the condensate behave as a single, coherent quantum entity — like a "super-atom." This leads to macroscopic quantum phenomena, such as superfluidity and interference patterns. Plasma is a separate state where electrons are stripped from atoms, but BEC is not plasma. Thus, BEC is neither a solid nor a condensed solid; it is a unique, quantum-mechanical state of matter. Answer: Bose-Einstein Condensate is the fifth state of matter . © examsnet.com

Question: The rate of evaporation of liquid does not depend upon
Option_B: its surface area exposed to the atmosphere
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Evaporation rate depends on factors that affect how easily molecules escape from the liquid surface. It does not depend on the total mass of the liquid. Explanation: Evaporation is a surface phenomenon. Molecules at the surface need enough energy to break free into the air. The rate of evaporation increases with higher temperature because molecules gain more energy. A larger surface area allows more molecules to escape at once, increasing the rate. High humidity means the air already contains many water vapor molecules, which slows evaporation. Wind removes vapor near the surface, making it easier for molecules to escape and thus speeds up evaporation. The mass of the liquid does not directly affect the evaporation rate. For a fixed surface area and environmental conditions, the rate (mass lost per unit time) stays the same regardless of total mass. Only time to completely evaporate changes with mass, not the rate itself. Answer: C. its mass © examsnet.com

Question: Rutherford's alpha particle scattering experiment on thin gold foil was responsible for the discovery of ________.
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Rutherford's alpha scattering experiment showed that atoms contain a small, dense, positively charged nucleus. Explanation: Rutherford directed a beam of alpha particles at a thin gold foil. Most alpha particles passed straight through without deflection. A few were deflected by large angles, and some even bounced back. This unexpected deflection indicated a tiny, massive, and positively charged core inside the atom. Rutherford called this core the atomic nucleus. The earlier plum pudding model, which described the atom as a uniform sphere of positive charge with embedded electrons, was disproved. Thus, the experiment led to the discovery of the atomic nucleus. Electrons were discovered earlier by J.J. Thomson (1897). Protons were discovered by Goldstein and later identified by Rutherford (1919). Neutrons were discovered by James Chadwick (1932). Answer: C. atomic nucleus © examsnet.com

Explanation: Solution: Concept: A food chain describes the linear sequence of organisms where each organism eats the one below it, transferring energy through food. Explanation: The term “food chain” refers to the unidirectional flow of energy from producers (plants) to consumers and then to decomposers. Each step in this sequence is called a trophic level. Energy is lost at each level, so only about 10% passes to the next. Thus, the correct definition is the passage of food (and the energy it contains) from one organism to another. Answer: Option C: passage of food (and thus energy) from one organism to another. © examsnet.com

Question: Which one of the following is active transport?
Option_A: It is the movement of a substance against a diffusion gradient with the use of energy from respiration.
Option_B: It is the movement of a substance against a diffusion gradient without the use of energy.
Option_C: It is the movement of a substance against a diffusion gradient with the use of energy from photosynthesis.
Option_D: It is the movement of a substance along a diffusion gradient with the use of energy from respiration.
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Active transport is the movement of substances across a cell membrane against their concentration gradient, requiring cellular energy (ATP) usually derived from respiration. Explanation: In active transport, molecules move from a region of lower concentration to a region of higher concentration. This movement is against the diffusion gradient, so it is not spontaneous. Energy is needed to overcome the gradient; this energy comes from the breakdown of ATP during cellular respiration. Passive transport (like facilitated diffusion) moves substances along the gradient without energy. Photosynthesis provides energy in plants, but the universal immediate energy source for active transport is ATP from respiration. Thus, the correct description is: movement against the diffusion gradient using energy from respiration. Answer: Option A: It is the movement of a substance against a diffusion gradient with the use of energy from respiration. © examsnet.com

Question: Chlorophyll in photosynthetic prokaryotic bacteria is associated with ________.
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Photosynthetic prokaryotes lack chloroplasts and have chlorophyll attached to membranous vesicles formed from plasma membrane infoldings. Explanation: In eukaryotic plants, chlorophyll is located inside plastids called chloroplasts. Photosynthetic bacteria such as cyanobacteria are prokaryotes, so they lack membrane‑bound organelles like chloroplasts. These bacteria possess invaginations of the plasma membrane that create membranous vesicles (also known as thylakoids). Chlorophyll and other pigments are embedded in these membranous vesicles to perform photosynthesis. Therefore, chlorophyll in photosynthetic prokaryotic bacteria is associated with membranous vesicles. Answer: B. membranous vesicles © examsnet.com

Question: What do you mean by 'Demographic Dividend'?
Option_A: A rise in the rate of economic growth due to a higher share of working age people in a population
Option_B: A rise in the rate of literacy due to development of educational institutions in different parts of the country
Option_C: A rise in the standard of living of the people due to the growth of alternative livelihood practices
Option_D: A rise in the gross employment ratio of a country due to government policies
Explanation: Solution: Concept: The economic growth potential from a shift in age structure, when the working-age population (15-64) is larger than the non-working-age share. Explanation: Definition: The United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) defines demographic dividend as the economic growth potential arising from changes in a population's age structure. It occurs when the proportion of working-age people (typically 15 to 64 years) exceeds the proportion of dependents (children 0-14 and elderly 65+). A larger workforce can boost productivity and savings, leading to faster economic growth. India has one of the youngest populations globally. By 2020, India's median age was only 28, compared to 37 in China and the USA, 45 in Western Europe, and 49 in Japan. According to the Economic Survey 2018-19, India's demographic dividend is expected to peak around 2041, when the working-age group (20-59 years) will reach 59% of the population. The broader 15-59 age group is projected to hit 65% in 2036. Answer: A rise in the rate of economic growth due to a higher share of working-age people in a population (Option A). © examsnet.com

Question: What is Inter-cropping?
Option_A: It is the time period between two cropping seasons.
Option_B: It is growing of two or more crops in random mixture.
Option_C: It is growing of two or more crops in definite row patterns.
Option_D: It is growing of different crops on a piece of land in a pre-planned succession
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Inter-cropping is an agricultural practice where two or more crops are grown simultaneously on the same field in a definite row pattern. Explanation: In inter-cropping, rows of one crop alternate with rows of another crop in a planned arrangement. Example: soybean + maize, or finger millet (bajra) + cowpea (lobia). Crops are chosen so that their nutrient requirements differ. This ensures better use of soil nutrients and reduces the spread of pests and diseases. It differs from mixed cropping, where crops are sown randomly without a row pattern (e.g., wheat + gram). Mixed cropping is a risk management strategy, while inter-cropping follows a specific pattern for higher yield. Sequence cropping (or crop rotation) is growing different crops in succession on the same land. The recall period refers to the gap between two cropping seasons. Answer: Option C – It is growing of two or more crops in definite row patterns. © examsnet.com

Question: Which one of the following cell organelles is known as 'suicide bags' of a cell?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Lysosomes contain digestive enzymes that destroy the cell when it gets damaged, so they are called the 'suicide bags' of the cell. Explanation: Lysosomes are small, single-membrane sacs filled with strong hydrolytic enzymes. These enzymes break down foreign materials and worn-out cell parts. Question: The value of the slope of a normal demand curve is ________.
Explanation: Solution: Concept: The slope of a normal demand curve indicates the rate at which quantity demanded changes as price changes; it is always negative due to the law of demand. Explanation: A normal demand curve slopes downward from left to right. This shows an inverse relationship between price and quantity demanded. As price increases, quantity demanded decreases, so the slope is negative. Mathematically, slope is Δ P Δ Q \frac{\Delta P}{\Delta Q} Δ Q Δ P ​ (rise over run). Since P P P and Q Q Q move in opposite directions, the numerator and denominator have opposite signs, giving a negative value. Options like positive, zero, or infinity apply only to special cases (e.g., Giffen goods, perfectly elastic demand, or perfectly inelastic demand), not to a normal demand curve. Question: Which one of the following is an example of a price floor?

Question: Consider the following statements: 1. Particles of matter intermix on their own. 2. Particles of matter have force acting between them. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Question: If the speed of a moving magnet inside a coil increases, the electric current in the coil
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Electromagnetic induction states that the induced voltage (emf) depends on the rate of change of magnetic flux through the coil. Explanation: When a magnet moves into a coil, it changes the magnetic flux linking the coil. A faster movement increases the rate of change of flux. Question: Rajya Sabha has exclusive jurisdiction in

Question: The term soil impoverishment relates to which one of the following?
Option_C: Soil getting very deficient in plant nutrients
Option_D: Soil getting enriched with plant nutrients
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Soil impoverishment refers to the condition where soil becomes severely lacking in essential plant nutrients. Explanation: The term "soil impoverishment" describes a decline in soil fertility. It occurs when nutrients vital for plant growth are removed or depleted. This can happen due to continuous cropping, leaching, or microbial competition. For example, excessive addition of certain nutrients can cause microbes to monopolize nitrogen, leaving less for plants. This contrasts with soil erosion, which is the physical removal of topsoil by wind or water. Soil deposition is the addition of sediment to a landmass, not nutrient loss. Soil enrichment is the opposite process, where nutrients are added. Thus, impoverishment specifically means the soil becomes very deficient in plant nutrients. Answer: C. Question: Which one of the following is the correct sequential phase in the successional development of vegetation community in a habitat?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: The succession of a vegetation community follows a fixed sequence of stages: Nudation, Migration, Reaction, and Stabilization. Explanation: Succession begins with Nudation , where a bare area is created by disturbances like glacial recession, erosion, or climatic changes. Next is Migration , where seeds, spores, or other propagules reach the bare area through wind, water, or animals. Then comes Reaction , where the growing vegetation modifies the habitat (e.g., soil, light, moisture) through its own activities. Finally, Stabilization occurs when certain species become well-adapted and persist, leading to a relatively stable community (climax). Thus, the correct order is Nudation → Migration → Reaction → Stabilization. Answer: Option C: Nudation, Migration, Reaction and Stabilization. © examsnet.com

Question: In graphite, each carbon atom is bonded to three other carbon atoms
Option_B: in the same plane giving a hexagonal array

Explanation: Solution: Concept: Graphite has a layered structure where each carbon atom is covalently bonded to three others in a planar hexagonal arrangement. Explanation: Each carbon atom in graphite undergoes s p 2 sp^2 s p 2 hybridization. It forms three sigma bonds with three neighbouring carbon atoms in the same plane. These bonds create a hexagonal (six-membered) ring pattern, like a honeycomb. The fourth valence electron is delocalised, allowing electrical conductivity. The layers are stacked and held by weak van der Waals forces. This planar hexagonal array is unique to graphite among carbon allotropes. Question: Soap solution used for cleaning purpose appears cloudy. This is due to the fact that soap micelles can
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Soap micelles form colloidal-sized particles that scatter light, giving the solution a cloudy appearance. Explanation: Soap molecules in water assemble into micelles—spherical clusters with hydrophobic tails inward and hydrophilic heads outward. These micelles are large enough (typically 10 10 10 – 1000 1000 1000 nm) to act as colloidal particles. When light passes through the solution, these particles cause the Tyndall effect—scattering of light in all directions. This scattered light makes the solution appear cloudy or bluish. The cloudiness is not due to refraction, diffraction, or polarization, but solely due to the scattering of light by the dispersed micelles. Answer: B. scatter light © examsnet.com

Question: People prefer to wear cotton clothes in the summer season. This is due to the fact that cotton clothes are
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Cotton clothes help keep the body cool by absorbing sweat and promoting evaporation. Explanation: In summer, the body sweats to regulate temperature. Cotton fibres are hydrophilic – they absorb moisture (sweat) readily. The absorbed sweat spreads on the fabric, increasing its surface area for evaporation. Evaporation requires latent heat of vaporization ( L L L ), which is taken from the body. This removal of heat lowers the skin temperature, providing a cooling effect. So, the key property is that cotton is a good absorber of water. It does not directly convey, radiate, or absorb heat; it absorbs water to enable evaporative cooling. Answer: Option A – good absorbers of water. © examsnet.com

Question: Employing Chromatography, one cannot separate
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Chromatography is a physical separation method based on differential distribution between stationary and mobile phases. It cannot separate isotopes because isotopes have nearly identical chemical properties and thus behave identically in chromatographic processes. Explanation: Isotopes of the same element have the same electronic configuration and chemical reactivity. Chromatography relies on differences in affinity, solubility, or adsorption, which do not vary between isotopes. Thus, techniques like diffusion, distillation, centrifugation, thermal diffusion, exchange reactions, or electrolysis are used for isotope separation, not chromatography. In contrast, chromatography can separate colours from a dye, pigments from natural colour, and drugs from blood because these have distinct chemical structures and interact differently with the stationary and mobile phases. Answer: Option A: radio‑isotopes. © examsnet.com

Question: Consider the following statement: "An atomic number of an element is a more fundamental property than its atomic mass." Who among the following scientists has made the above statement?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: The statement that atomic number is more fundamental than atomic mass is based on Moseley’s work with X‑rays, which redefined the periodic law. Explanation: Mendeleev arranged elements by increasing atomic mass. This led to anomalies like isotopes and wrong order of some elements. Henry Moseley studied X‑ray spectra and found that each element’s characteristic X‑ray frequency is related to its atomic number ( Z Z Z ). He proved that atomic number (number of protons) is the true basis of periodicity, not atomic mass. This gave the modern periodic law: properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic numbers. Thus, Moseley is credited with the statement that atomic number is a more fundamental property than atomic mass. Answer: B. Henry Moseley © examsnet.com

Question: Which one of the following acids is also known as Vitamin C?

Question: Marsilea, Fern and Horse-tail are examples of which one of the following plant groups?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Pteridophytes are vascular plants that reproduce via spores and do not produce seeds or flowers. Explanation: Marsilea, Fern, and Horse-tail (Equisetum) are all examples of Pteridophytes. They possess true roots, stems, and leaves with vascular tissues (xylem and phloem). Gymnosperms (e.g., Cycas, Pinus) are seed plants with naked seeds, while angiosperms (e.g., Rose, Mango) are flowering plants with enclosed seeds. Question: The property of the sound waves that determines the pitch of the sound is its
Explanation: Solution: Concept: The pitch of a sound is directly determined by its frequency, which is the number of vibrations per second. Explanation: Pitch is the perceptual quality that allows us to classify a sound as high or low. A higher frequency produces a higher pitch, while a lower frequency produces a lower pitch. The unit of frequency is hertz (Hz), where 1 Hz = 1 vibration per second 1 \text{ Hz} = 1 \text{ vibration per second} 1 Hz = 1 vibration per second . Amplitude, wavelength, and intensity do not affect pitch. Amplitude is the maximum displacement of particles from the mean position and relates to loudness. Wavelength is the distance between successive compressions or rarefactions and is inversely related to frequency via v = f λ v = f \lambda v = f λ (speed of sound). Intensity is the power per unit area carried by the wave and is perceived as loudness, not pitch. Thus, among the given options, only frequency governs pitch. Answer: A. frequency © examsnet.com

Explanation: Solution: Concept: A plane mirror forms a virtual, erect, and laterally inverted image of the same size as the object. Explanation: The image in a plane mirror is always virtual, meaning it cannot be projected onto a screen. It is erect (upright) and of the same size as the object. The image is laterally inverted — the left and right sides are swapped. The distance of the image behind the mirror equals the distance of the object in front of the mirror. Among the given options, the statement that the image is real is incorrect because plane mirrors only produce virtual images. Thus, option C is not true. The lower mirror then reflects the light horizontally into the observer’s eye. This setup allows the observer to see objects that are not in a direct line of sight. The periscope works on the principle of reflection of light. It is commonly used in submarines and armoured vehicles. Answer: The two plane mirrors are kept parallel to each other . © examsnet.com

Question: Which one of the following types of radiation has the shortest wavelength?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: The electromagnetic spectrum orders radiation by wavelength, with shorter wavelengths corresponding to higher energy. Explanation: Among the given options, ultraviolet (UV) rays have the shortest wavelength. Explanation: Solution: Concept: An epidemic disease spreads rapidly among a population in a short time. Some diseases do not have epidemic potential because of their transmission pattern. Explanation: Cholera, malaria, and smallpox are classic examples of epidemic diseases. Cholera (caused by V i b r i o c h o l e r a e Vibrio\ cholerae Vib r i o c h o l er a e ) spreads through contaminated water. Malaria (caused by P l a s m o d i u m Plasmodium Pl a s m o d i u m parasite) is transmitted by mosquitoes and can cause outbreaks. Question: Which one of the following is the correct sequence of events during sexual reproduction in plants?

Option_C: Pollination, fertilization, division of zygote, formation of embryo, seedling
Option_D: Seedling, formation of embryo, division of zygote, pollination, fertilization
Explanation: Solution: Concept: The correct sequence of events in sexual reproduction of flowering plants is pollination, fertilization, division of zygote, embryo formation, and finally seedling germination. Explanation: Pollination is the transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma. Fertilization occurs when the male gamete (from pollen) fuses with the egg cell in the ovule, forming a zygote. The zygote then undergoes repeated cell divisions (cleavage) to form a multicellular embryo. The embryo develops inside the seed and, under suitable conditions, germinates to become a seedling. Answer: Option C: Pollination, fertilization, division of zygote, formation of embryo, seedling. © examsnet.com

Question: Which one of the following is the 'energy currency' for cellular processes?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: The molecule that stores and supplies immediate energy for cellular activities is called the energy currency of the cell. Explanation: Adenosine triphosphate ( A T P \mathrm{ATP} ATP ) is the universal energy carrier in living organisms. When a cell needs energy, it breaks the terminal phosphate bond of A T P \mathrm{ATP} ATP to form A D P \mathrm{ADP} ADP (adenosine diphosphate) and releases energy. This energy is used for processes like muscle contraction, active transport, and biosynthesis. A T P \mathrm{ATP} ATP is produced mainly during respiration, especially in mitochondria, which are known as the “powerhouses” of the cell. Glucose is a source of energy but must be broken down to generate A T P \mathrm{ATP} ATP . A D P \mathrm{ADP} ADP is the lower-energy form, and pyruvic acid is an intermediate in energy metabolism, not the direct currency. Question: The electromagnetic waves, which are used for satellite communication, are
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Radio waves are the electromagnetic waves best suited for satellite communication due to their long wavelength and ability to penetrate the atmosphere without significant absorption. Explanation: The electromagnetic spectrum includes radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X‑rays, and gamma rays. Each type has a specific frequency and wavelength range. Question: Which one of the following is the correct sequence of organs that occur in the path of urine flow in human body?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: The correct anatomical path of urine flow in the human excretory system is: kidneys produce urine, which is transported via ureters to the urinary bladder for storage, and finally expelled through the urethra. Explanation: Urine is formed in the kidneys after blood filtration. From each kidney, urine flows into a ureter. The ureters are two tubes that carry urine down to the urinary bladder. The urinary bladder stores urine temporarily. During urination, urine passes from the bladder into the urethra and out of the body. Thus, the sequence is: kidney → ureter → urinary bladder → urethra. This order matches option A. Answer: Kidney, ureter, urinary bladder, urethra (Option A). © examsnet.com

Question: Which of the following endocrine glands is not found in pair in humans?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Most endocrine glands exist in pairs in the human body, but the pituitary gland is a single, unpaired gland. Explanation: The pituitary gland is a pea-sized gland located in a bony cavity at the base of the brain. It is attached to the hypothalamus and is often called the master gland because it controls many other glands. Unlike the adrenal glands (one above each kidney), testes (paired in males), and ovaries (paired in females), the pituitary is a single structure. It secretes several hormones such as growth hormone, prolactin, thyroid-stimulating hormone, melanocyte-stimulating hormone, and oxytocin. None of these functions require a paired organ; the pituitary works as one gland. Therefore, among the given options, only the pituitary gland is not found in pairs in humans. Answer: B. Pituitary © examsnet.com

Question: Who among the following scientists introduced the concept of immunization to the medical world?

Other scientists in the options: Robert Koch discovered germs of tuberculosis, cholera, and anthrax, a founder of modern bacteriology. Robert Hooke was a polymath known for microscopy. Question: Which one of the following Acts reserved seats for women in Legislatures in accordance with the allocation of seats for different communities?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: The Government of India Act, 1935 extended communal representation by introducing separate electorates for women and other groups. Explanation: The Government of India Act, 1935 was a major constitutional reform in British India. It introduced the principle of separate electorates for women, along with depressed classes (scheduled castes) and labour (workers). This meant women could vote for and elect candidates from reserved seats allocated specifically for them, based on community representation. The Act further extended voting rights to about 10 % 10\% 10% of the total population. It also abolished provincial dyarchy and introduced provincial autonomy. Other features included the establishment of the Reserve Bank of India, a Federal Court, and federal/state public service commissions. The earlier Acts — the Government of India Act, 1858, the Indian Councils Act, 1909, and the Government of India Act, 1919 — did not provide such reserved seats for women. Question: Which one among the following was demanded by the All India Depressed Classes Leaders' Conference at Bombay in 1931?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: The All India Depressed Classes Leaders' Conference in Bombay in 1931, led by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, demanded separate electorates for untouchables to secure political representation. He founded organisations like the Bahishkrit Hitkarini Sabha (1924) and launched movements like the Mahad Satyagraha (1927) for public water access. At the All India Depressed Classes Leaders' Conference in Bombay (May 1931), a major demand was separate electorates for untouchables. This demand aimed to ensure that depressed classes could elect their own representatives, rather than relying on reserved seats within general electorates. Other options: Universal adult suffrage (A) was a broader demand not specific to this conference; Reserved seats for minorities (C) was a later concept; A unitary state (D) was not a primary demand here. The demand for separate electorates eventually led to the Poona Pact (1932), where Gandhi's fast forced a compromise — reserved seats instead of separate electorates. Dwarakanath Tagore was a businessman and philanthropist, not associated with the founding of this art society. Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyaya was a novelist and poet, best known for composing "Vande Mataram", and had no role in founding the society. Question: Who among the following Sultans succeeded in finally breaking and destroying the power of Turkan-i-Chihalgani?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: The Turkan-i-Chihalgani, or “Corps of Forty,” was a group of powerful Turkish nobles created by Iltutmish. Balban later dismantled their influence. Explanation: Iltutmish formed the Turkan-i-Chihalgani to consolidate his rule. After his death, these nobles became too powerful and often dominated weak sultans. Balban, as the next strong ruler, understood the threat they posed. He systematically reduced their power by executing or sidelining them. Question: Who among the following Mongol leaders/commanders did not cross Indus to attack India?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: The Mongol leader who never crossed the Indus River into India was Chenghiz Khan, while his successors did invade. Explanation: During the Sultanate period, the Indus served as the cultural boundary, but the actual line of defence lay west of it. Chenghiz Khan pursued the Khwarizmi prince Jalal-ud-din to the Indus after a battle. Jalal-ud-din jumped his horse into the river and escaped into India. Although Chenghiz Khan camped near the Indus for three months, he chose not to cross into Indian territory. He returned to Mongolia and died in 1227. Delhi Sultan ruler Iltutmish refused to shelter Jalal-ud-din, and while Chenghiz Khan was alive, the Mongols did not expand into the northwest. Intensive subsistence agriculture, however, focuses on producing enough food for the farmer's own family, with little or no surplus for trade. Question: The Cash Reserve Ratio refers to
Option_A: the share of Net Demand and Time Liabilities that banks have to hold as liquid assets
Option_B: the share of Net Demand and Time Liabilities that banks have to hold as balances with the RBI
Option_C: the share of Net Demand and Time Liabilities that banks have to hold as part of their cash reserves
Option_D: the ratio of cash holding to reserves of banks
Explanation: Solution: Concept: The Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) is the portion of a bank's total deposits (Net Demand and Time Liabilities) that it must keep as a deposit with the central bank (RBI). Explanation: CRR is a monetary policy tool used by the RBI to control money supply and inflation. Banks cannot use this amount for lending or investment; it is held only as a balance with the RBI. When inflation is high, the RBI increases CRR to reduce the funds available for banks to lend, thus slowing down economic activity. The current CRR rate (as of May 2020) is 3.00% of NDTL. This regulation is under the authority of the central bank (RBI), which handles monetary policy, not fiscal policy (managed by the Ministry of Finance). Comparing the options: Option A describes SLR (Statutory Liquidity Ratio), not CRR. Option B correctly states that CRR is the share of NDTL held as balances with the RBI. Option C is vague and incorrect because CRR is not part of the bank's own cash reserves held in vaults—it is a deposit with RBI. Option D incorrectly defines CRR as a ratio of cash holding to reserves. Answer: Option B – the share of Net Demand and Time Liabilities that banks have to hold as balances with the RBI. © examsnet.com

Question: Amitabh Bachchan was recently conferred with the prestigious Dada Saheb Phalke Award. Who among the following was the first recipient of the award?

It is named after Dadasaheb Phalke, who directed India’s first full-length feature film, Raja Harishchandra (1913). Question: The famous Mughal painting, depicting Jahangir embracing the Safavid king Shah Abbas, was painted by which one of the following Mughal painters?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Identifying the Mughal painter of the famous allegorical portrait depicting Emperor Jahangir embracing Safavid king Shah Abbas. Explanation: The painting "Jahangir Embracing Shah Abbas" is a celebrated Mughal miniature. An inscription on the miniature records that Jahangir himself commissioned the artist Abu’l Hasan (also known as Abul Hasan) to paint this scene, based on a dream the emperor had. The artwork shows both rulers in traditional costumes, embracing each other in a friendly manner. The likeness of Shah Abbas was taken from portraits made by Bishandas, who accompanied the Mughal embassy to Iran in 1613. This gave a sense of realism to a fictional meeting, because the two monarchs never actually met. Therefore, the painter of this famous work was Abul Hasan, and not Bishandas (who only provided reference portraits). Answer: Option B: Abul Hasan. © examsnet.com
