For example, titles like Gautamiputra (son of Gautami) and Vashishthiputra (son of Vashishthi) directly link the king’s name to his mother. The Mallas, Vidhehas, and Yaudheyas were republican or monarchical states that did not follow matronymic naming. Thus, the Satavahanas uniquely identified themselves through their mother’s lineage. Question: Which one of the following statements about the famous text of panchatantra is correct?
Option_A: It is a philosophical text reflecting the debates of the time and refuting rival positions.
Option_B: It is a text ushering in linguistics as a formal science
Option_C: It is a text discussing developments in various spheres of natural sciences
Option_D: It is a text showing through illustration what should and should not be done
Explanation: Solution: Concept: The Panchatantra is a collection of fables that uses stories to illustrate moral and practical lessons. Explanation: The text is a famous ancient Indian work attributed to Vishnusharman. It is structured as a series of interconnected stories where animals and humans act out dilemmas. Each story demonstrates through example what is wise (should do) and what is unwise (should not do). For instance, it covers topics like forming alliances, waging war, and splitting alliances. Thus, it is a "Nirdarshana" — a work that shows by illustration. Other options: Philosophical texts debate and refute rival views; linguistics as a formal science was pioneered by Sanskrit grammarians; natural science developments are found in texts like Shulvasutras and Ganit-shastras. Answer: Option D: It is a text showing through illustration what should and should not be done. © examsnet.com

Question: Geomorphic factors influencing plant and animal distributions are
Option_C: slope angle, slope aspect and relief
Option_D: slope angle, slope aspect and relative relief
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Geomorphic factors are landform characteristics that affect the distribution of plants and animals by influencing microclimate, soil, and habitat. Explanation: The key geomorphic factors are: • Slope angle (or steepness): affects sunlight exposure, erosion, and drainage. • Slope aspect (orientation relative to north): influences insolation, moisture, and temperature. • Relative relief (difference in elevation between divide and valley): determines habitat diversity and microclimates. Slope angle alone or only slope aspect and relief are incomplete. All three together shape the physical environment that supports life. Thus, the correct set is slope angle, slope aspect, and relative relief. Answer: Option D – slope angle, slope aspect and relative relief. © examsnet.com

Question: Which one of the following groups of cities does not have Sclerophyll as its natural vegetation cover?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Sclerophyll vegetation is characteristic of Mediterranean climate regions around the world. Explanation: Sclerophyll forests and shrublands are found in regions with a Mediterranean climate – mild, wet winters and hot, dry summers. These regions include the Mediterranean Basin, California, central Chile, the Cape Region of South Africa, and southwestern Australia. Now examine each group of cities: • Valparaiso (Chile) and Cape Town (South Africa) – both lie in Mediterranean climate zones, so sclerophyll is present. • Lisbon (Portugal, Mediterranean Basin) and Perth (southwestern Australia) – both have sclerophyll vegetation. • Los Angeles (California) and Adelaide (south Australia, Mediterranean climate) – both support sclerophyll. • Las Vegas (Nevada, USA) has a hot desert climate, not Mediterranean. Queensland (northeastern Australia) has a tropical/subtropical climate, not Mediterranean. Neither supports sclerophyll as natural cover. Thus, only the last pair lacks sclerophyll vegetation. Answer: Option D – Las Vegas and Queensland. © examsnet.com

Question: In the Hadley cell thermal circulation, air rises up and finally descends at
Explanation: Solution: Concept: The Hadley cell is a tropical atmospheric circulation where warm air rises near the equator and sinks at about 30° latitude, forming subtropical high-pressure zones. Explanation: In the Hadley cell, air heated at the equator rises and moves poleward at high altitude. As it travels, it cools and becomes denser. Around 30° north and south latitude, the cold air descends toward the surface. This descending air creates a belt of high pressure known as the subtropical high-pressure cells. These cells are responsible for dry, stable conditions and major desert regions. The intertropical convergence zone (ITCZ) and doldrums are areas of rising air near the equator, not descending air. Equatorial troughs also refer to the low-pressure region near the equator. Thus, the correct location of sinking air in the Hadley cell is the subtropical high-pressure cells. Answer: subtropical high-pressure cells © examsnet.com

Question: Which one of the following soils is characterized by very high content of organic matter?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Histosols are soils composed primarily of organic matter, formed in waterlogged conditions. Question: Overseas Indians can exercise franchise in an election to the Lok Sabha under which of the following condition? 1. They must be citizens of India. 2. Their names must figure in the electoral roll. 3. They must be present in India to vote. Select the correct answer using the code given below.
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Overseas Indians (NRIs) can vote in Lok Sabha elections only if they are Indian citizens, registered in the electoral roll, and physically present in India on polling day. Explanation: Statement 1 is correct because only a citizen of India is eligible to vote. An overseas elector must not have acquired citizenship of any other country. Statement 2 is correct: the person’s name must appear in the electoral roll of the constituency where his/her Indian residence (as per passport) is located. This is governed by Section 20A of the Representation of the People Act, 1950. Statement 3 is also correct. Currently, India does not permit e-voting for NRIs. Postal ballots are available only for election duty personnel, armed forces, and preventive detention cases. Proxy voting is allowed only for specific categories (armed forces, police, government officials posted abroad). Therefore, an ordinary overseas Indian voter must be present at the polling station in India and show the original passport to cast a vote. All three conditions are mandatory. Answer: 1, 2 and 3 © examsnet.com

Question: Which of the following are considered to be the four pillars of human development?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: The four pillars of human development are the core principles that guide the expansion of opportunities and well-being for all people. Explanation: The four pillars defined in the human development framework are: Equity (sometimes termed equality), Sustainability , Productivity , and Empowerment . • Equity means giving everyone fair access to opportunities, regardless of gender, race, income, or caste. • Sustainability ensures that present development does not compromise the ability of future generations to meet their own needs. • Productivity focuses on enhancing people’s knowledge, health, and skills to increase their efficiency and contribution. • Empowerment involves enabling people, especially disadvantaged groups, to participate in decisions and improve their lives through good governance and policies. These four pillars form the foundation of the human development approach, as established by Mahbub ul Haq. Answer: Option B: Equality, productivity, empowerment and sustainability (where equality is used synonymously with equity). © examsnet.com

Question: Which one of the following was added as a fundamental right through the Constitution (86th Amendment) Act, 2002?
Option_A: To strive towards excellence in individual and collective activity
Option_B: To provide opportunities for education to one's child between the age of 6 and 14 years
Option_C: To work for the welfare of women and children
Explanation: Solution: Concept: The 86th Amendment Act, 2002 added the right to free and compulsory education for children as a fundamental right. Explanation: This amendment inserted Article 21 A 21A 21 A into the Indian Constitution. It makes education a fundamental right for all children between the ages of 6 6 6 and 14 14 14 years. The state is now obligated to provide free and compulsory education to every child in this age group. Additionally, it also added a new fundamental duty under Article 51 A ( k ) 51A(k) 51 A ( k ) for parents or guardians to provide education opportunities to their child. Thus, the correct option is the one that mentions providing opportunities for education to one's child between 6 6 6 and 14 14 14 years. Question: Which one of the following Articles of the Constitution of India provides a person right against double jeopardy?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Article 20 of the Indian Constitution grants protection against double jeopardy. Explanation: Double jeopardy means a person cannot be prosecuted and punished twice for the same offence. This fundamental right is specifically guaranteed under Article 20(2) of the Constitution. It is part of the six fundamental rights listed in Part III (Articles 12–35) of the Indian Constitution. Article 20 also protects against ex-post-facto laws and self-incrimination. Other Articles mentioned in the options cover different rights: Article 21 (right to life), Article 22 (protection against arrest), and Article 23 (prohibition of forced labour). Thus, only Article 20 provides the right against double jeopardy. Answer: Option A, Article 20. © examsnet.com

Question: Consider the following statements about the Stone Age in India: 1. Different periods are identified on the basis of the type and technology of stone tools. 2. There are no regional variations in the type and technology of tools in different periods. 3. Stone Age cultures of different periods evolved uniformly in a near unilinear fashion all over the subcontinent. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: The Stone Age in India is classified into distinct periods based on the technological evolution of stone tools, but regional variations existed. Explanation: Statement 1 is correct because the three main periods—Palaeolithic, Mesolithic, and Neolithic—are defined by the type and manufacturing technique of stone implements. Statement 2 is false: tool types and technologies varied across different regions of India due to differences in raw material availability, climate, and cultural practices. Statement 3 is false: Stone Age cultures did not evolve uniformly; there were regional differences in the timing and sequence of cultural developments. Answer: 1 only (Option A) © examsnet.com

Question: From which one of the following factory sites were limestone and chert blades mass produced and sent to various Harappan settlements in Sindh?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Harappan civilization had specialized centers for mass-producing stone tools like chert and limestone blades, which were then traded to other settlements. Explanation: The Rohri Hills and Sukkur region in Sindh had abundant high-quality chert and limestone deposits. Archaeological evidence shows that these sites were factories where blades were mass-produced using specialized techniques. These finished blades were then sent to various Harappan settlements across Sindh for everyday use. Other sites like Khetri (copper) or Chagai Hills (stone tools) are not primarily known for limestone and chert blade production and distribution. Thus, the correct source is the Sukkur and Rohri Hills. Answer: Sukkur and Rohri Hills (Option A). © examsnet.com

The second volume focuses on Bengal's history from Aurangzeb's death, including the English relations with the nawabs and the rise of British supremacy. The third volume deals with the Nizam of Hyderabad, Haidar Ali, Nawab-Wazirs of Oudh, and Ahmad Shah Abdali's invasions. Explanation: Solution: Concept: The Tattvabodhini Sabha was a progressive society founded by Debendranath Tagore in 1839. Explanation: Solution: Concept: Article 32 of the Constitution guarantees the right to move the Supreme Court for enforcement of fundamental rights. Explanation: The Supreme Court can issue writs like habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto, and certiorari for enforcing fundamental rights. If the petitioner's grievance does not involve any fundamental right, the remedy under Article 32 is not available. Other grounds, such as availability of alternative remedy, disputed facts, or incorrect writ choice, do not bar the Supreme Court from granting relief under Article 32. Explanation: Solution: Concept: The power of the Supreme Court to hear a dispute for the first time, not on appeal, is called original jurisdiction. Question: With whom did Subhas Chandra Bose form an alliance to destroy the Holwell Monument in Calcutta during 1939-40?

Question: Which one among the following was India's first trade union in the proper sense of the term?

This union is considered the first organised trade union in India because it had a proper structure, collective bargaining goals, and sustained worker participation. The workers went on strike against the managing company Binny & Co., which marked a key event in Indian labour history. Question: Who among the following formed the Seva Samiti Boy Scouts Association in 1914?

Question: Which of the following Articles in the Constitution of India are exceptions to the Fundamental Rights enumerated in Article 14 and Article 19?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Specific articles in Part III of the Constitution shield certain laws from being challenged under the right to equality (Article 14) and the right to freedom (Article 19). Explanation: The correct pair of articles that are exceptions to Article 14 and Article 19 is Article 31A and Article 31C. Article 31A protects laws relating to the acquisition of estates and similar reforms from being invalidated on the grounds of violating Article 14 or Article 19. Article 31C, inserted by the 25th Amendment (1971), gives effect to Directive Principles under Articles 39(b) and 39(c) and also is immune from challenge under Article 14 and Article 19. Therefore, any law falling under these two articles cannot be struck down by a court for contravening the fundamental rights of equality and freedom. Option A is correct because only Article 31A and Article 31C specifically provide this immunity together. Option B (Article 31B and Article 31D) is incorrect: Article 31B protects laws in the Ninth Schedule but not expressly against Article 14 and 19 only, and Article 31D does not exist as a specific exception. Option C (Article 12 and Article 13) provides definitions and the doctrine of judicial review, not exceptions. Option D (Article 16 and Article 17) are substantive fundamental rights themselves, not exceptions. Answer: Option A: Article 31A and Article 31C © examsnet.com

Question: Which one of the following is not the necessary condition for the issue of a writ of Quo Warranto?

Option_C: The office must not be a substantive one.
Option_D: There has been a contravention of the Constitution or a Statute in appropriating such person to that office.
Explanation: Solution: Concept: The writ of Quo Warranto challenges the legal authority of a person holding a public office. Explanation: A writ of Quo Warranto can be issued only if the office is a substantive public office of a permanent character. It must be created by a statute or the Constitution. The office must be public, not private or ministerial. There must be a contravention of the Constitution or a statute in the appointment. The condition "The office must not be a substantive one" is false. In fact, the office must be substantive – it cannot be merely a temporary or ministerial role. Therefore, this option is not a necessary condition for the writ. Answer: Option C: The office must not be a substantive one. © examsnet.com

Explanation: Solution: Concept: Article 338A of the Indian Constitution specifically establishes the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST) as a constitutional body. Explanation: The 89th Amendment Act, 2004 inserted Article 338A into the Constitution. Therefore, when the price of a commodity falls, there is normally no shift in the demand curve. Answer: Option A – price of a commodity falls. © examsnet.com

Question: A market, in which there are a large number of firms, homogeneous product, infinite elasticity of demand for an individual firm and no control over price by firms, is termed as________. \text{A market, in which there are a large number of firms, homogeneous product, infinite elasticity of demand for an individual firm and no control over price by firms, is termed as\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_.} A market, in which there are a large number of firms, homogeneous product, infinite elasticity of demand for an individual firm and no control over price by firms, is termed as________.
Explanation: Solution: Concept: This market structure is defined by many firms, identical products, and firms being price takers with perfectly elastic demand. Explanation: In perfect competition, there are a large number of small firms. All firms sell a homogeneous (identical) product. The demand curve facing an individual firm is perfectly elastic (horizontal). This means the firm can sell any quantity at the prevailing market price. The firm has no control over price; it must accept the market-determined price. Thus, the firm is a price taker, not a price maker. Other characteristics include free entry and exit, perfect knowledge, and no selling costs. These features match the description given in the question exactly. Answer: Perfect competition (Option D). © examsnet.com

Question: Which one of the following was not a demand made by the Congress moderates?
Option_D: Higher jobs for Indians in the army
Explanation: Solution: Concept: The Congress moderates made several constitutional, administrative, and economic demands, but extension of Permanent Settlement was not among them. Explanation: The moderates demanded expansion of legislative councils at central and provincial levels. They wanted elected Indian members in these councils and control over the public purse. They demanded self-rule within the British Empire, like the self-governing colonies of Australia and Canada. They asked for Indian representation in the Viceroy's Executive Council and the Governors' councils. They demanded universal adult franchise with direct election of legislative council members. They demanded spread of primary education and improvement of the police system. Gorge is a deep, narrow valley with very steep sides, formed by river erosion. Braided channels occur when a river deposits sediment and splits into multiple interwoven channels due to high sediment load. Canyon is a deep, narrow valley with steep, step‑like sides, formed by river erosion in horizontally bedded sedimentary rocks. The Grand Canyon is a famous example of a canyon. Since gorge, braids, and canyon are all products of river action, they are fluvial landforms. Only cirque is formed by glacial action, making it the non‑fluvial landform. Answer: Cirque (Option A) © examsnet.com

Question: At the Gandhar School of Art, initially, blueshists and green fightlights were used. When did plaster completely replace stone as the main material used by the sculptors of the Gandhara school?

Plaster allowed for more detailed and free-standing structures like chaityas, viharas, and stupas. Question: Al-Birunì's Kitab-ul-Hind was written in which language?

Question: Which of the following statements with regard to the privileges of the Members of the Parliament are correct? 1. Explanation: Solution: Concept: Parliamentary privileges are special rights and immunities enjoyed by MPs collectively and individually, distinct from ordinary citizens' rights under Article 19(1)(a). Question: Which one of the following statements with regard to·the appointment of the Members of the Parliamentary Committees is correct?

Question: Which of the following were added to the Preamble of the Constitution of India by the Constitutional Amendment, 1976? 1. Socialist 2. Secular 3. Integrity 4. Fraternity Select the correct answer using the code given below.

Lower courts (subordinate courts) do not have the power to issue writs. Only the Supreme Court and High Courts are constitutionally empowered to issue writs such as habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, certiorari, and quo warranto. Question: Which one of the following statements with regard to ultra violet light is NOT correct?

Explanation: Solution: Concept: Ultraviolet (UV) light is a type of electromagnetic radiation with properties distinct from longitudinal waves. Explanation: UV light is an electromagnetic wave, so it is transverse, not longitudinal. In transverse waves, particle oscillations are perpendicular to the direction of wave travel. EM waves, including UV light, can travel through a vacuum (no medium required). The wavelength of UV light ranges from about 10 10 10 nm to 400 400 400 nm, which is shorter than visible light ( 400 − 700 400-700 400 − 700 nm). Therefore, the statements "It is an electromagnetic wave", "It can travel through vacuum", and "Its wavelength is shorter than that of visible light" are all correct. Question: If the speed of light in air is represented by e e e and the speed in a medium is u u u , then the refractive index of the medium can be calculated using the formula_______.
Explanation: Solution: Concept: The refractive index of a medium is the ratio of the speed of light in vacuum (or air) to the speed of light in that medium. Explanation: When light passes from one medium to another, its speed changes. The refractive index n n n quantifies how much the light bends. It is defined as n = speed of light in vacuum speed of light in the medium n = \frac{\text{speed of light in vacuum}}{\text{speed of light in the medium}} n = speed of light in the medium speed of light in vacuum ​ . Therefore, the refractive index n = e u n = \frac{e}{u} n = u e ​ . Hence, the correct formula is e e e divided by u u u . This matches option B. Question: Under the Kingdom Plantae, which of the following individuals are predominantly aquatic?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Algae are the predominantly aquatic members of Kingdom Plantae, belonging to the subgroup Thallophyta. Explanation: Kingdom Plantae is divided into five subgroups: Thallophyta, Bryophyta, Pteridophyta, Gymnosperms, and Angiosperms. Algae belong to Thallophyta and are mostly aquatic, living in freshwater or marine environments. They contain chlorophyll and perform photosynthesis. Examples include S p i r o g y r a Spirogyra Sp i ro g yr a , U l o t h r i x Ulothrix U l o t h r i x , C l a d o p h o r a Cladophora Cl a d o p h or a , and C h a r a Chara C ha r a . Bryophytes (mosses, liverworts) are terrestrial but grow in moist habitats. Pteridophytes (ferns, horsetails) are also terrestrial and prefer shady, damp places. Gymnosperms are seed-producing plants that are fully terrestrial. Thus, among the given options, only algae are predominantly aquatic. Answer: B. Algae © examsnet.com

Question: All the individuals of a particular organism, such as rose plants, belong to a taxonomic category called __________ \text{All the individuals of a particular organism, such as rose plants, belong to a taxonomic category called \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_} All the individuals of a particular organism, such as rose plants, belong to a taxonomic category called __________
Explanation: Solution: Concept: All individuals of a single kind of organism belong to the species, the most basic taxonomic unit. Explanation: Taxonomic categories range from broad (kingdom) to specific (species). A species includes all individuals that can interbreed and produce fertile offspring. For example, all humans belong to the species Homo sapiens . Similarly, all rose plants of the same kind (e.g., Rosa indica ) are grouped into one species. The genus Rosa contains many different rose species, not just a single organism type. Therefore, the category for "all the individuals of a particular organism" is species. Answer: Species. © examsnet.com

Question: Pearls are harvested from __________ \text{Pearls are harvested from \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_} Pearls are harvested from __________
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Pearls are formed inside the shell of certain mollusks, primarily oysters, as a natural defense against irritants. Explanation: Pearls are harvested from oysters, specifically marine oysters and freshwater mussels. When an irritant like a grain of sand or parasite enters the oyster's shell, the oyster secretes layers of nacre (mother-of-pearl) around it. This process forms a natural pearl. Cultured pearls are produced similarly by farmers intentionally inserting an irritant into the mollusk. Pearls are composed of aragonite and conchiolin in thin layers. The quality depends on the thickness and number of layers, affecting refraction, reflection, and diffraction of light. Oysters are the primary source of harvested pearls. Answer: Oyster. © examsnet.com

Question: Wings of birds and bats are considered analogous structures because they have ________. \text{Wings of birds and bats are considered analogous structures because they have \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_.} Wings of birds and bats are considered analogous structures because they have ________.
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Analogous structures have different evolutionary origins but perform similar functions. Explanation: The wings of birds and bats are analogous organs. This means they evolved separately but serve the same purpose—flight. Bird wings have feathers along the arm, while bat wings are skin flaps stretched between bones. Their structural dissimilarity shows they are not inherited from a common winged ancestor. Natural selection led to convergent evolution, producing similar functions despite different origins. Answer: different origin and common function © examsnet.com

Question: Apart from hyper acid secretion, peptic ulcers are also developed due to bacterial infection. The causative agent is __________.
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Peptic ulcers can be caused by bacterial infection, most commonly by Helicobacter pylori . Explanation: Peptic ulcers are sores in the stomach lining, esophagus, or small intestine. They are often due to stomach acid damage, but bacterial infection is another major cause. Helicobacter pylori is a spiral-shaped bacterium that can penetrate the stomach's protective mucus layer. It survives in the acidic environment and causes chronic inflammation, leading to ulcers. Other bacteria like E. coli , Streptococcus pneumoniae , and Salmonella typhimurium cause different diseases (food poisoning, pneumonia, typhoid). They are not associated with peptic ulcers. Answer: A. Helicobacter pylori © examsnet.com

Question: Which of the following combinations of source and screen would produce the sharpest shadow of an opaque object?
Option_A: A point source and an opaque screen
Option_B: An extended source and an opaque screen
Option_C: A point source and a transparent screen
Option_D: An extended source and a transparent screen
Explanation: Solution: Concept: A sharp shadow forms when a point light source and an opaque screen are used, as rays travel in straight lines and do not scatter or pass through the screen. Explanation: A point source emits light in all directions from a single, small point (e.g., a lit candle). Light rays from a point source diverge but remain well-defined. When an opaque object blocks these rays, a distinct region of darkness forms behind it. The opaque screen stops all light, making the shadow clearly visible. An extended source (like a tube light) emits rays from many points, causing fuzzy edges (penumbra). A transparent screen allows light to pass through, preventing a shadow from forming entirely. Therefore, the combination of a point source and an opaque screen produces the crispest shadow. Answer: Option A: A point source and an opaque screen. © examsnet.com

Question: Which one of the following statements about phloem is correct?
Option_D: Phloem gives support to the plant.
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Phloem is a living vascular tissue that transports organic nutrients (photosynthetic products) from leaves to other plant parts. Explanation: Phloem consists of sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem fibres, and phloem parenchyma. Sieve tubes are elongated living cells that carry carbohydrates, mainly sucrose, from leaves to roots and fruits. Companion cells regulate the activity of adjacent sieve elements and help in loading/unloading sugars. Phloem fibres provide commercial utility due to pliability and strength, but the primary function is conduction. Phloem parenchyma (transfer cells) assist in food conveyance near leaf veinlets. Thus, phloem transports organic compounds synthesized during photosynthesis — not water and minerals (xylem’s role). It is a complex tissue (not simple), and its support function is secondary. Hence, the correct statement is that phloem transports photosynthetic products. Answer: B. Phloem transports photosynthetic products. © examsnet.com

Question: In human beings, the chromosomes that determine birth of a normal female child are ________. \text{In human beings, the chromosomes that determine birth of a normal female child are \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_.} In human beings, the chromosomes that determine birth of a normal female child are ________.

Option_B: one X chromosome from mother and one Y chromosome from father
Option_C: two X chromosomes from mother and one X chromosome from father
Option_D: one X chromosome and one Y chromosome from father and one X chromosome from mother
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Human sex is determined by the combination of sex chromosomes ( X \mathrm{X} X and Y \mathrm{Y} Y ) inherited from each parent. Explanation: Human cells normally have 23 pairs of chromosomes, including one pair of sex chromosomes. Females have two X \mathrm{X} X chromosomes ( X X \mathrm{XX} XX ), while males have one X \mathrm{X} X and one Y \mathrm{Y} Y chromosome ( X Y \mathrm{XY} XY ). A mother always contributes an X \mathrm{X} X chromosome to her child. A father contributes either an X \mathrm{X} X or a Y \mathrm{Y} Y chromosome. If the child receives an X \mathrm{X} X from the father, the pair becomes X X \mathrm{XX} XX — resulting in a female. If the child receives a Y \mathrm{Y} Y from the father, the pair becomes X Y \mathrm{XY} XY — resulting in a male. Therefore, for a normal female child, the required chromosomes are one X \mathrm{X} X from the mother and one X \mathrm{X} X from the father. This matches option A. Answer: Option A – one X \mathrm{X} X chromosome from mother and one X \mathrm{X} X chromosome from father. © examsnet.com

Question: Antibiotic such as penicillin blocks _______ \text{Antibiotic such as penicillin blocks \_\_\_\_\_\_\_} Antibiotic such as penicillin blocks _______
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Penicillin is a beta-lactam antibiotic that inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis. Explanation: Penicillin blocks the enzyme transpeptidase, which is responsible for cross-linking peptidoglycan chains in the bacterial cell wall. This prevents the formation of a rigid cell wall, causing the bacterium to undergo osmotic lysis and die. Penicillin is bactericidal and is most effective against actively growing Gram-positive bacteria. It does not affect RNA synthesis, DNA synthesis, or cell division directly. Answer: cell wall formation in bacteria © examsnet.com

Question: Which one of the following is used for storing biological tissues?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Cryopreservation uses ultra-cold, inert liquids to halt biological activity and preserve tissues without damage. Explanation: Liquid nitrogen ( N 2 \mathrm{N}_2 N 2 ​ ) boils at −196°C, making it ideal for storing biological tissues. Liquid nitrogen is widely used in biobanks, fertility clinics, and research labs for preserving sperm, eggs, embryos, and other tissues. Liquid helium ( H e \mathrm{He} He ) is colder (−269°C) but far more expensive and not practical for routine tissue storage. Liquid argon ( A r \mathrm{Ar} Ar ) has a boiling point of −186°C, is inert, but less commonly used for biological preservation. Explanation: The atomic number of phosphorus is 15 15 15 . This shows five valence electrons in the 3 s 3s 3 s and 3 p 3p 3 p subshells. To reach a stable octet (like argon), phosphorus can gain three electrons, giving a valency of 3 3 3 . Alternatively, it can lose all five valence electrons, showing a valency of 5 5 5 . Phosphorus also has vacant 3 d 3d 3 d orbitals. In an excited state, one electron from 3 s 3s 3 s is promoted to 3 d 3d 3 d , giving 3 s 1 3 p 3 3 d 1 3s^{1}3p^{3}3d^{1} 3 s 1 3 p 3 3 d 1 . Now there are five unpaired electrons, allowing phosphorus to form five bonds (valency 5 5 5 ). Hence, phosphorus shows variable valency: 3 3 3 and 5 5 5 . Explanation: Solution: Concept: Arabica, Robusta and Liberica are commercially grown species of coffee beans. Robusta has a stronger taste and higher caffeine content. Liberica is less common, with a distinct fruity and woody flavour. These three varieties are grown in many coffee-producing countries worldwide. Answer: Coffee © examsnet.com

Question: Aluminium is manufactured from _____.
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Bauxite is the primary ore from which aluminium is extracted industrially. Explanation: Aluminium is a reactive metal and does not occur free in nature. It is manufactured by processing its ore, bauxite. Bauxite is a sedimentary rock rich in hydrous aluminium oxides, such as gibbsite ( A l 2 O 3 ⋅ 3 H 2 O \mathrm{Al}_2\mathrm{O}_3 \cdot 3\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} Al 2 ​ O 3 ​ ⋅ 3 H 2 ​ O ), boehmite ( A l 2 O 3 ⋅ H 2 O \mathrm{Al}_2\mathrm{O}_3 \cdot \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} Al 2 ​ O 3 ​ ⋅ H 2 ​ O ), and diaspore ( A l 2 O 3 ⋅ H 2 O \mathrm{Al}_2\mathrm{O}_3 \cdot \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} Al 2 ​ O 3 ​ ⋅ H 2 ​ O ). The extraction involves two main steps: the Bayer process to purify bauxite into alumina ( A l 2 O 3 \mathrm{Al}_2\mathrm{O}_3 Al 2 ​ O 3 ​ ), followed by the Hall–Héroult electrolytic process to reduce alumina to pure aluminium. Other ores listed, such as copper ore (for copper), mica ore (for sheet silicates), and manganese ore (for manganese), do not contain economically recoverable levels of aluminium. Thus, bauxite is the correct and only viable source for aluminium manufacture. Answer: Bauxite ore. © examsnet.com

Question: Which one of the following sea ports gained significance for handling iron-ore exports to Japan?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Mormugao port in Goa became the key hub for exporting iron ore to Japan after its modernization in 1961. Explanation: Mormugao, a natural harbour at the Zuari estuary, was remodeled in 1961 to handle large-scale iron-ore exports. It is one of the oldest ports on India's west coast and has breakwater protection. During the financial year 2010-11, it recorded the highest-ever iron-ore exports, primarily to Japan. Other ports like Kandla (Gujarat), Ennore (Tamil Nadu), and Kochi (Kerala) are not specifically associated with iron-ore exports to Japan. Answer: Mormugao © examsnet.com

Question: Which one of the following is not a function of money?
Option_A: Act as an intermediate in the exchange process
Option_B: Acts as a store of value
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Money serves three primary functions: medium of exchange, unit of account, and store of value. Regulating consumption is not a function of money. Explanation: Money's core functions include acting as a medium of exchange to facilitate transactions, as a unit of account to measure value, and as a store of value to preserve purchasing power over time. Option A ("Act as an intermediate in the exchange process") is the medium-of-exchange function. Option B ("Acts as a store of value") is a standard function. Option C ("Used as the unit account") is the unit-of-account function. Option D ("Used for regulating consumption") is not a recognized function of money. Consumption regulation is a policy goal, not an inherent monetary function. Answer: Option D: Used for regulating consumption © examsnet.com

Question: The situation where the equilibrium level of real GDP falls short of potential GDP is known as _________.
Explanation: Solution: Concept: A recessionary gap occurs when actual real GDP is less than potential GDP at full employment. Explanation: The equilibrium level of real GDP is the output determined by aggregate demand and supply. Potential GDP is the maximum output an economy can produce at full employment. When equilibrium real GDP falls short of potential GDP, the economy is operating below its capacity. This shortfall creates downward pressure on prices and leads to higher unemployment. Policymakers may use expansionary fiscal or monetary policies to close this gap. This situation is known as a recessionary gap (or contractionary gap). It contrasts with an inflationary gap, where actual GDP exceeds potential GDP. Thus, the correct term is recessionary gap. Answer: A. Recessionary gap © examsnet.com

Question: The excess of total expenditure of Government over its total receipts, excluding borrowings, is known as
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Fiscal deficit measures the government's total borrowing requirement in a financial year. Explanation: Fiscal deficit is the difference between the government's total expenditure and its total receipts, excluding borrowings. Total receipts include revenue receipts (tax and non-tax) and non-debt capital receipts (like loan recoveries). Borrowings are not counted as receipts because they are used to cover the deficit. Thus, fiscal deficit = total expenditure – (revenue receipts + recovery of loans + other non-debt capital receipts). Answer: Fiscal deficit © examsnet.com

Question: Exchange rates state the value of one currency in terms of other currencies. Which one of the following statements with respect to the exchange rate of a currency is correct?
Option_A: Floating exchange rates are rates in which the Governments interfere by buying or selling their currencies
Option_B: Fixed exchange rates are rates set by Government decisions and Maintained by Government actions.
Option_C: Under the Bretton Woods System, the exchange rates are floated in terms of rise or fall in price of gold.
Option_D: Under the classical gold standard, the exchange rates are fixed in terms of price of dollar.
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Exchange rate regimes can be fixed or floating based on how the value is determined. Explanation: Option A is incorrect because floating exchange rates are determined by market forces (supply and demand), not by government interference. Government intervention is a managed float. Option B is correct because fixed exchange rates are officially set and maintained by government or central bank actions (e.g., buying/selling reserves, adjusting interest rates). Option C is incorrect: Under the Bretton Woods System, exchange rates were fixed against the US dollar, which was pegged to gold at $ 35 \$35 $35 per ounce. Rates were not floated based on gold price. Option D is incorrect: Under the classical gold standard, each currency had a fixed gold parity, so exchange rates were fixed in terms of gold, not in terms of the dollar. Answer: Fixed exchange rates are rates set by Government decisions and Maintained by Government actions. © examsnet.com

Question: Francois Bernier was physician to __________.
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Francois Bernier, a French physician and traveler, served as a personal physician to a Mughal prince. Explanation: Francois Bernier was a French physician, political philosopher, and historian who visited the Mughal Empire during the 17th century. He served as a physician to Prince Dara Shikoh, the eldest son and heir-apparent of Emperor Shah Jahan. Dara Shikoh was a liberal and scholarly prince, favored by his father and his sister Princess Jahanara. Bernier later wrote the book "Travels in the Mogul Empire," which provides valuable insights into Mughal history. In his account, he mentions the execution of Dara Shikoh in 1659 during the war of succession with Aurangzeb. Other individuals like Prince Murad (a son of Akbar) and Princess Jahanara (Dara's sister) were not his patrons. Answer: Prince Dara Shikoh © examsnet.com

Question: Which one of the following British firms was taken over by Soorajmull-Nagarmull group?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: The Soorajmull-Nagarmull group, a Marwari business family, expanded into jute manufacturing and acquired several British firms in Calcutta during the 1940s. In the 1940s, their group moved into jute manufacturing and bought jute companies controlled by McLeod and Co. McLeod and Co. owned ten jute mills, sixteen tea companies, and light railways at that time. Thus, the British firm taken over by the Soorajmull-Nagarmull group was McLeod. Answer: A. McLeod © examsnet.com

Question: Which one of the following statements with regard to the ryotwari settlement is not correct? ​
Option_A: In southern and western India, the ryotwari settlement was adopted.
Option_B: Ryotwari was in principle a direct contract between the ryot and the state.
Option_C: It means a tax contract valid for usually 30 years.
Option_D: In principle, it strengthened the former elite, the zamindars and weakened the peasantry.
Explanation: Solution: Concept: The ryotwari settlement was a British land revenue system that made a direct contract between the state and the individual cultivator (ryot), eliminating middlemen. Explanation: It was adopted in large parts of southern and western India, such as the Madras and Bombay Presidencies. Under this system, the revenue was directly collected from the ryot, who was considered the owner of the land. The tax assessment was valid for a fixed period, usually 30 years, after which it was revised. No zamindars or other intermediaries were involved; the state dealt directly with the peasants. Therefore, the ryotwari system actually weakened the former elite (zamindars) and strengthened the peasantry by giving them ownership rights. Thus, the statement that it strengthened the zamindars and weakened the peasantry is false. The other three statements are correct: ryotwari was adopted in southern and western India, it was a direct contract between ryot and state, and the tax contract was usually for 30 years. Answer: Option D is not correct. © examsnet.com

Question: Which one of the following statements about the British Indian Medical Service (IMS) is not correct?​
Option_B: It recruited health professionals by means of a competitive examination.
Option_C: Indians were never admitted to IMS.
Option_D: The IMS was at first meant to look after the troops
Explanation: Solution: Concept: The British Indian Medical Service (IMS) was a military medical body, but Indians were indeed admitted to it, making the claim of their exclusion false. Explanation: The IMS began in 1764 as a medical department for the troops and servants of the East India Company. Thus, statements A and D are correct. Recruitment was done via competitive examination, so statement B is also correct. However, Indians were admitted to the IMS; the first Indian officer, Soorjo Coomar Goodeve Chuckerbutty, joined on 24 January 1855, followed by Rajendra Chandra Chandra on 27 January 1858. Hence, statement C—“Indians were never admitted to IMS”—is not correct. Answer: The incorrect statement is option C. © examsnet.com

Question: When was the monopoly of China trade lost by East India Company ?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: The East India Company's monopoly over trade with China was ended by a Parliamentary Act in 1833. Explanation: The East India Company held a monopoly on trade with China for many years. However, British merchants and companies wanted free trade and petitioned the government. In 1813, the company's monopoly over trade with India was abolished, but the China trade monopoly remained. Finally, in 1833, the Charter Act of 1833 completely abolished the company's monopoly over all trade, including with China. This opened the China trade to all British companies. After 1833, opium smuggling from India to China became a major business for private British firms. Answer: 1833 (Option B). © examsnet.com

Question: National Disaster Management Authority is headed by
Explanation: Solution: Concept: The National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) is the apex body for disaster management in India, and its chairperson is the Prime Minister. Explanation: The NDMA was established under the Disaster Management Act of 2005. The Act designates the Prime Minister of India as the ex-officio chairperson of the NDMA. The NDMA is responsible for laying down policies, plans, and guidelines for disaster management. It coordinates the enforcement of these policies and approves national and state-level disaster management plans. The Home Minister, President, or Health Minister do not head the NDMA. Thus, the correct authority is the Prime Minister. Answer: The Prime Minister (Option A). © examsnet.com

Question: Which of the following statements regarding the ‘casting vote’ in the Parliament is/are correct ? 1. It is cast by the speaker or a person acting as such. 2. It is cast in addition to voting in the first instance. 3. It is cast in the case of equality of votes. 4. It is always cast to maintain the status quo. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Casting vote is a special vote cast by the Speaker or Chairman only when votes are tied. Explanation: Statement 1 is correct because the casting vote is cast by the Speaker (Lok Sabha) or Chairman (Rajya Sabha), or any person acting in that role. Statement 2 is incorrect: the Speaker does not have an ordinary vote; the casting vote is not in addition to a prior vote but is exercised only once when ties occur. Statement 3 is correct: the casting vote is used exactly in case of equality of votes. Statement 4 is incorrect: although convention may often lean to maintain status quo, the Speaker/Chairman is not bound to always vote to preserve the status quo – they can vote either way. Thus, only statements 1 and 3 are correct. Answer: B. 1 and 3 only © examsnet.com

Question: Equality before the law or equal protection of the laws within the territory of India is guaranteed under which one of the following Articles of the Constitution of India ?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Equality before law and equal protection of laws are guaranteed in Part III of the Indian Constitution. Explanation: The right to equality is protected under Articles 14 to 18 of the Constitution. Article 14 is the most significant among them. It states: "The State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India." This means every person living in India has an equal right before the law, and equals must be treated equally. Article 14 has two parts: equality before law and equal protection of laws. It also includes two tests of classification: intelligible differentia and rational relation with the object of the act. Other articles listed are: • Article 15: prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth. • Article 16: guarantees equal opportunity in public employment. • Article 22: protects against arbitrary arrest and preventive detention. Answer: Article 14 © examsnet.com

Question: 'Legal Positivism' theory was developed by
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Legal positivism is the theory that law is a social construct based on commands from a sovereign, separate from morality. Explanation: John Austin developed this theory to treat law as a true science. He defined law as a command issued by a sovereign and backed by sanctions. The core idea is the separation thesis, which states that law and morality are conceptually distinct. Legal positivism argues that the existence of a law depends on its source, not its moral merit. Austin’s work emphasizes that law reflects relations of power and obedience. This philosophy does not dismiss moral evaluation of law but separates it from legal validity. Answer: John Austin © examsnet.com

Question: Who among the following said that Democracy means a system of ‘Government by Consent’?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: John Locke argued that legitimate government derives its authority from the consent of the governed. Explanation: Locke’s political philosophy, especially in his *Two Treatises of Government* (1689), rejects absolute monarchy. He claims that people form a political society by voluntarily agreeing to be ruled for the common good. This agreement, or social contract, establishes government by the consent of the people. Thus, democracy is understood as a system where rulers derive their power from the people’s consent. Other thinkers like J.S. Mill, Bentham, or Rousseau do not use the exact phrase “government by consent” in this specific manner. Answer: John Locke (Option A). © examsnet.com

Question: Milpa and Ladang are different names for
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Milpa and Ladang are regional names for shifting cultivation, an agricultural practice where land is cleared, farmed briefly, and then left fallow to restore fertility. Explanation: Shifting cultivation is also known as slash‑and‑burn agriculture. Farmers clear a patch of forest, grow crops for a few years, and then move to a new area once the soil loses nutrients. The original plot is abandoned for several years to naturally regain fertility. Different regions call this practice by different names. Milpa is the term used in Yucatan (Mexico) and Guatemala. Ladang is commonly used in Indonesia, Malaysia, and parts of Southeast Asia. Similarly, in India it is called Jhoom in Assam, Podu in Andhra Pradesh and Odisha, and Bewar in Madhya Pradesh. In other parts of the world, names include Ray (Vietnam), Roka (Brazil), and Konuko (Venezuela). The key features of shifting cultivation include use of fire, rotational fields, simple tools, and mixed cropping. Answer: Option A: Shifting cultivation is the correct answer. © examsnet.com

Question: Which one of the following approaches of human development was initially proposed by the International Labour Organisation (ILO) and emphasised on health, education, food, water supply, sanitation and housing ?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: The International Labour Organisation (ILO) proposed the basic needs approach, which directly targets essential requirements for human development such as health, education, food, water supply, sanitation, and housing. Explanation: The ILO introduced this approach at the 1976 World Employment Conference. It defined basic needs to include food, clothing, housing, education, and public transportation. Unlike the income approach, which equates development with higher per capita income, the basic needs approach sets specific production targets to meet these needs directly. Unlike the welfare approach, which relies on government expenditure on welfare amenities, the basic needs approach emphasises active participation and employment as both means and ends. Unlike the capability approach associated with Amartya Sen, which focuses on building health, education, and resource access capabilities, the basic needs approach originally framed by the ILO centres on the provision of minimum material and social requirements. Therefore, the focus on health, education, food, water supply, sanitation, and housing exactly matches the ILO's basic needs framework. Answer: B. Basic needs approach © examsnet.com

Question: Which one of the following elements is a non-metal but is lustrous?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Non-metals are usually dull in appearance, but iodine is an exception as it has a metallic lustre. Explanation: Most non-metals do not have a shiny or reflective surface. Iodine crystals, however, appear shiny and metallic when observed in solid form. That is why iodine is considered a non-metal that is lustrous. Carbon can be lustrous in its diamond allotrope, but the element carbon in its common forms (like graphite or amorphous carbon) is not consistently lustrous. Silicon and germanium are metalloids, not pure non-metals, and they exhibit some metallic properties but are not classified as non-metals. Therefore, among the given options, only iodine fits the description of a non-metal that is lustrous. Answer: Iodine © examsnet.com

Question: Which one of the following metals has both malleability and ductility properties:
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Malleability (ability to be hammered into thin sheets) and ductility (ability to be drawn into wires) are mechanical properties of metals that depend on their atomic structure and bonding. Explanation: Gold ( A u \mathrm{Au} Au ) is the most malleable and ductile of all metals. It can be hammered into sheets thin enough to transmit light and drawn into a single-atom-wide wire. Sodium ( N a \mathrm{Na} Na ) is soft and highly reactive, so it lacks significant malleability and ductility. Cerium ( C e \mathrm{Ce} Ce ) is a lanthanide metal that is relatively brittle and not particularly malleable or ductile. Mercury ( H g \mathrm{Hg} Hg ) is a liquid at room temperature, so it has no malleability or ductility at all. Only gold exhibits both properties to an exceptional degree. Answer: The metal with both malleability and ductility properties is A u \mathrm{Au} Au (gold). © examsnet.com

Question: We are given three copper wires of different lengths and different areas of cross-section. Which one of the following would have highest resistivity ?
Option_A: Copper wire of 50 cm length and 1 mm diameter
Option_B: Copper wire of 25 cm length and 0-5 mm diameter
Option_C: Copper wire of 10 cm length and 2-0 mm diameter
Option_D: All the wires would have same resistivity
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Resistivity is an intrinsic property of a material that depends only on the material's nature and temperature, not on its length or cross-sectional area. Explanation: Resistivity ( ρ \rho ρ ) is constant for a given material at a fixed temperature. Even though resistance ( R R R ) changes with length ( L L L ) and area ( A A A ) according to R = ρ L A R = \rho \frac{L}{A} R = ρ A L ​ , the resistivity ρ \rho ρ itself remains unchanged. All three wires are made of copper, so they have the same resistivity. The different lengths (50 cm, 25 cm, 10 cm) and diameters (1 mm, 0.5 mm, 2.0 mm) do not affect resistivity. Therefore, all wires have identical resistivity. Answer: All the wires would have the same resistivity (Option D). © examsnet.com

Question: Which of the following statements about ‘fission’ is correct ? 1. It is related with the creation of new individuals by means of cell division in unicellular organism. 2. It is related with the transformation of heavier nuclei into smaller nuclei. 3. It is related with the creation of a heavier nuclei by means of combining two higher nuclei. Select the correct answer using the code given below :
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Fission refers to two distinct processes: biological fission (cell division) and nuclear fission (splitting of atomic nuclei). Explanation: Statement 1 is about biological fission. In unicellular organisms, fission is the process where a single cell divides to form new individuals. This statement is correct. Statement 2 is about nuclear fission. It is the process where a heavy atomic nucleus splits into two or more smaller nuclei, releasing a huge amount of energy. This statement is correct. Statement 3 describes nuclear fusion, where two lighter nuclei combine to form a heavier nucleus. That is not fission, so statement 3 is incorrect. Thus, statements 1 and 2 are correct. Answer: Option C: 1 and 2 only. © examsnet.com

Question: Which one of the following is an electric conductor ?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: The human body conducts electricity due to the presence of ions in its fluids. Explanation: Electric conductors allow electric current to pass through them. Plastic sheets, distilled water, and wooden sheets are poor conductors (insulators). Distilled water lacks dissolved ions, so it does not conduct electricity. The human body, however, contains about 70% water with dissolved ions such as N a + \mathrm{Na}^+ Na + , K + \mathrm{K}^+ K + , and C l − \mathrm{Cl}^- Cl − . These ions are mobile and can carry charge, making the body a good conductor. This is why electric shocks can be dangerous—the current flows easily through the body. Therefore, among the given options, only the human body acts as an electric conductor. Answer: C. Human body © examsnet.com

Question: A non-spherical shining spoon can generally be considered as a
Explanation: Solution: Concept: A spoon’s shiny surface is curved, not flat, so it behaves as a curved mirror with a spherical shape. Explanation: A plane mirror has a flat reflective surface. A spoon, even if not perfectly spherical overall, has a curved bowl. The reflecting surface of a spoon approximates part of a sphere. Hence it is classified as a spherical mirror (concave on the front, convex on the back). A parabolic mirror has a different curve, and a lens is transparent. Therefore a non‑spherical shining spoon is generally considered a spherical mirror. Answer: Spherical mirror © examsnet.com

Question: Who amongst the following is a pioneer in discovering the heating effect of electric current?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: The heating effect of electric current was discovered by James Prescott Joule through his experiments on the equivalence of mechanical, electrical, and heat energy. Explanation: Joule established that heat produced in a current-carrying wire is proportional to the square of the current and the resistance. His law is stated as P = I 2 R P = I^{2}R P = I 2 R , where P P P is power (heat per second in watts), I I I is current in amperes, and R R R is resistance in ohms. This discovery proved that electrical energy can be converted into heat energy. Other scientists listed did not focus on this specific effect: Isaac Newton studied motion and gravity; Galileo Galilei studied motion and astronomy; J. J. Thomson discovered the electron and proposed a model of the atom. © examsnet.com

Question: Which one of the following laws of electromagnetism does not give the direction of magnetic field ?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Faraday's law gives the magnitude of induced EMF, not the direction of any vector like magnetic field. Explanation: The right‑hand thumb rule directly shows the direction of magnetic field around a current‑carrying conductor. Fleming’s left‑hand rule gives the direction of force on a current‑carrying conductor; however, if current and force are known, it can also indicate the direction of magnetic field. Fleming’s right‑hand rule gives the direction of induced current; similarly, knowing motion and current lets one deduce the magnetic field direction. Faraday’s law of electromagnetic induction only quantifies the induced EMF ( E = − d Φ d t \mathcal{E} = -\frac{d\Phi}{dt} E = − d t d Φ ​ ). It does not provide any directional information about the magnetic field itself. Hence, among the given options, Faraday’s law is the one that does not give the direction of the magnetic field. Right-hand thumb rule When electricity (conventional current) flows in a long straight wire it creates a circular or cylindrical magnetic field around the wire. According to the right-hand rule. If the fingers of the right hand are curled in the direction of the circular component of the current, the right thumb points to the north pole. Answer: Option D © examsnet.com

Question: An antibiotic is not useful against a virus whereas a vaccine is. Which one of the following is the most appropriate reason for this ?
Option_A: An antibiotic can break RNA only, whereas virus has DNA.
Option_B: ​An antibiotic is a carbohydrate in its chemical nature, whereas a vaccine is a protein which works well to kill a virus.
Option_C: Only a vaccine can break the genetic material of a virus.
Option_D: A virus does not use biochemical pathways ​​which can be blocked by an antibiotic. But a vaccine can boost an immune system to fight the virus.
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Antibiotics target bacterial biochemical pathways, but viruses lack these pathways. Vaccines stimulate the immune system to recognize and fight viruses. Explanation: Antibiotics work by blocking specific biochemical processes in bacteria, such as cell wall synthesis or protein production. Viruses do not have their own independent metabolic machinery; they rely entirely on host cells to replicate. Therefore, antibiotics cannot disrupt viral activity because viruses do not use the same biochemical pathways. Vaccines, on the other hand, prepare the immune system by exposing it to harmless viral components. This allows the body to produce antibodies and memory cells that can quickly neutralize the actual virus upon infection. Thus, vaccines are effective against viruses while antibiotics are not. Answer: Option D: A virus does not use biochemical pathways which can be blocked by an antibiotic. But a vaccine can boost an immune system to fight the virus. © examsnet.com

Question: ‘Sleeping sickness' is caused by
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Sleeping sickness is a parasitic disease caused by protozoa of the genus Trypanosoma. Explanation: The causative agent is Trypanosoma brucei, transmitted by the tsetse fly (Glossina species). It is prevalent in sub-Saharan Africa. The parasite invades the central nervous system, leading to sleep disturbances and other neurological symptoms. Other options: Leishmania causes leishmaniasis, Plasmodium causes malaria, and Paramecium is a free-living ciliate, not pathogenic. Answer: Option A: Trypanosoma. © examsnet.com

Question: Which one among the following is a free living animal ?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Free-living animals are those that do not live on or inside another organism for nutrition; they are independent and not parasitic. Explanation: Among the given options, Planaria (class Turbellaria) is a free-living flatworm found in freshwater, marine, or terrestrial habitats. Liver fluke, Wuchereria, and Plasmodium are all parasitic organisms that depend on a host for survival. Liver fluke infects the liver of mammals; Wuchereria causes filariasis in humans; Plasmodium is the malaria parasite. Thus, Planaria is the only one that lives independently without requiring a host. Answer: Planaria (Option D) is the free-living animal. © examsnet.com

Question: Which one of the following is the Structure of a cardiac muscle cell ?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Cardiac muscle cells have a specific shape, branching pattern, and number of nuclei. Explanation: Cardiac muscle cells are cylindrical in shape. They are branched, allowing them to connect with neighbouring cells via intercalated discs. Each cardiac muscle cell typically contains a single nucleus (uninucleate). Question: Which one of the following naturally occurring acids is found in abundance in tomato ?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Tomatoes contain various organic acids, but citric acid is the most abundant. Explanation: Tomatoes naturally contain many acids, including citric, malic, oxalic, and ascorbic acid. Among these, citric acid is present in the highest concentration, giving tomatoes their characteristic tartness. Oxalic acid is also found in tomatoes, but in much smaller amounts compared to citric acid. Therefore, the acid found in abundance in tomato is citric acid, not oxalic acid or the others listed. Question: Which one of the following is used in soda-acid fire extinguishers?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: The soda-acid fire extinguisher uses a reaction that produces carbon dioxide gas to smother flames. Explanation: The main chemical used in a soda-acid fire extinguisher is sodium hydrogen carbonate (sodium bicarbonate). The extinguisher contains a solution of N a H C O 3 \mathrm{NaHCO}_3 NaHCO 3 ​ in water and a separate bottle of sulfuric acid ( H 2 S O 4 \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4 H 2 ​ SO 4 ​ ). When the knob is turned, the acid mixes with the bicarbonate solution. The reaction produces carbon dioxide gas: 2 N a H C O 3 + H 2 S O 4 → N a 2 S O 4 + 2 H 2 O + 2 C O 2 2\mathrm{NaHCO}_3 + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4 \rightarrow\mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{SO}_4 + 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} + 2\mathrm{CO}_2 2 NaHCO 3 ​ + H 2 ​ SO 4 ​ → Na 2 ​ SO 4 ​ + 2 H 2 ​ O + 2 CO 2 ​ Carbon dioxide is non-combustible and heavier than air. It forms a layer over the fuel, cutting off the oxygen supply. This simultaneously cools the material below its ignition temperature. Thus, the flame is extinguished without using water on electrical or oil fires. Other options: sodium chloride (table salt) does not produce C O 2 \mathrm{CO}_2 CO 2 ​ ; calcium hydroxide (lime) is a base; acetic acid (vinegar) is not used because it is weak and less effective. Answer: Sodium hydrogen carbonate (option B). © examsnet.com

Question: How many internal reflections of light take place in the formation of primary rainbow?

Question: Osmosis is the process of movement of water molecules from its​
Option_A: higher concentration to its lower concentration through a cell wall.
Option_B: lower concentration to its higher concentration through a semi-permeable membrane.
Option_C: higher concentration to its lower concentration through a fully permeable membrane.
Option_D: higher concentration to its lower concentration through a semi-permeable membrane.
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Osmosis is the net movement of water molecules from a region of higher water concentration to a region of lower water concentration through a semi‑permeable membrane. Explanation: In osmosis, the solvent (water) moves across a membrane that allows only water to pass. The driving force is the difference in water concentration (or water potential). Higher water concentration means fewer solute particles per unit volume (dilute solution). Lower water concentration means more solute particles (concentrated solution). Water naturally moves to equalize the concentration on both sides. The membrane must be semi‑permeable – it blocks solute molecules but lets water through. A fully permeable membrane would allow everything to pass, so not osmosis. A cell wall is not a selective barrier; the process specifically requires a semi‑permeable membrane. Answer: Option D: higher concentration to its lower concentration through a semi‑permeable membrane. © examsnet.com

Explanation: Solution: Concept: Structural unemployment occurs when there is a mismatch between the skills or location of workers and the requirements of available jobs. Question: The situation in an economy which is growing slowly along with rapid inflation (rising price level) is called
Explanation: Solution: Concept: The economic condition of slow growth combined with rapid inflation is called stagflation. Explanation: Stagflation occurs when an economy experiences both stagnant growth (high unemployment or slow GDP) and rising prices (inflation). It is distinct from stagnation (slow growth without inflation) and deflation (falling prices). This term became widely known in the 1970s when oil shocks caused many developed economies to face simultaneous inflation and recession. The misery index, the sum of inflation rate and unemployment rate, is often used to measure the discomfort caused by stagflation. Thus, the correct term matching the description is stagflation. Answer: C. Stagflation © examsnet.com

Question: Which one of the following statements about the Act V of 1843 relating to Slavery in India is correct ? ​
Option_A: It gave the masters the right to wilfully keep their slaves tied to their estates.
Option_B: It denied the masters the use of Courts to assert their claims on slaves.
Option_C: The Law Courts and masters worked jointly in resolving the cases of desertion.
Option_D: The slaves became the owners of the land.
Explanation: Solution: Concept: The Indian Slavery Act V of 1843 prohibited courts from enforcing any claims related to slavery, effectively denying masters legal recourse to recover slaves. Explanation: The Act was passed to implement the Law Commissioners' recommendation that slavery should not be legally recognised. Section 2 specifically declared that no Civil or Criminal Court or Magistrate could enforce any rights claimed over a person on the ground of slavery. This meant masters could no longer use the judicial system to assert ownership or recover runaway slaves. Section 1 forbade public auctions of slaves or their labour under court decrees or revenue demands. Section 3 protected property rights of ex-slaves, ensuring they could not be deprived of property simply because they had been slaves. Section 4 made it a criminal offense to harm any person on the pretext of them being a slave. Thus, the Act stripped masters of the legal power to enforce their claims through courts, which is exactly what option B states. Options A (tying slaves to estates), C (joint court-master action), and D (slaves becoming land owners) are not supported by the Act. Answer: Option B is correct: It denied the masters the use of Courts to assert their claims on slaves. © examsnet.com

Question: Which one of the following is the largest linguistic group of India?

It is set at 8 2 ∘ 3 0 ′ 82^\circ 30' 8 2 ∘ 3 0 ′ East longitude. This meridian passes through the centre of India, near Mirzapur in Uttar Pradesh. Question: Which one of the following is not a correct description of the Union Cabinet ?

Question: Which one of the following tributaries of river Indus feeds the canal system of the Bhakra Nangal Project?

Question: When the rivers discharge their waters from all directions into a lake or depression, the pattern is known as
Explanation: Solution: Concept: A drainage pattern where rivers flow from all directions into a central lake or depression is called centripetal drainage. Explanation: In a centripetal drainage system, water converges inward from surrounding highlands to a low-lying central basin. This pattern is common in enclosed basins or depressions where there is no outlet to the sea. It is also known as endorheic drainage, meaning water does not drain externally. Examples include Loktak Lake in Manipur, India, and many inland lakes in arid regions. Other drainage patterns are different: • Dendritic: resembles tree branches (e.g., rivers of the Northern Plains). • Radial: rivers flow outward from a central hill or mountain (e.g., Amarkantak range). • Trellis: parallel main rivers with short tributaries joining at right angles (e.g., glaciated valleys of Karakoram). Thus, when rivers discharge from all directions into a lake or depression, the pattern is centripetal. Answer: Centripetal © examsnet.com

Question: Which one of the following statements about the Coriolis force is not correct ?

Option_C: It deflects the wind to the right direction : in the southern hemisphere.
Option_D: It deflects the wind to the right direction in the northern hemisphere.
Explanation: Solution: Concept: The Coriolis force is an apparent force due to Earth's rotation that deflects moving objects (like wind) to the right in the northern hemisphere and to the left in the southern hemisphere. Explanation: The Coriolis force depends on latitude: it is maximum at the poles and zero at the equator. Thus, option A ("maximum at the poles") is correct. Option B ("absent at the equator") is also correct. Option D says the force deflects wind to the right in the northern hemisphere — this is true. However, in the southern hemisphere, the deflection is to the left, not to the right. Therefore, option C ("deflects the wind to the right in the southern hemisphere") is false. Answer: Option C is the incorrect statement. © examsnet.com

Question: In 1943, young leaders in which one of the following districts of Maharashtra set up parallel Government (Prati sarkar) with volunteer corps (Seva dals) and village units (tufan dals)?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: During the Quit India Movement, a parallel government (Prati Sarkar) was established in Satara district of Maharashtra in 1943. Explanation: The Satara Parallel Government operated from August 1943 to May 1946 as a guerrilla-style resistance against British rule. It was an armed offshoot of the 1942 Quit India Movement. Other parallel governments existed in Midnapore (Bengal), Ballia (Uttar Pradesh), Bhagalpur (Bihar), and Basudevpur (Odisha). The leader of the Satara Prati Sarkar was Krantisinh Nana Patil (1900–1976). Nana Patil later joined the Communist Party of India and was elected to the Lok Sabha from Satara in 1957 and from Beed in 1967. Question: Who founded the Central Hindu School at Benaras which was later developed into Benaras Hindu University ?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: The Central Hindu School in Varanasi was founded by a prominent theosophist and social reformer before being handed over for the establishment of Banaras Hindu University. Question: Article 231 of the Constitution of India grants power to establish a common High Court for two or more states to
Explanation: Solution: Concept: Article 231 of the Constitution empowers the Parliament to establish a common High Court for two or more states (or for states and a Union territory). Explanation: • Article 231 is located in Part VI (The States) of the Constitution. • It was substituted by the Constitution (7th Amendment) Act, 1956, and was not part of the original Constitution. • The Article states: "Parliament may by law establish a common High Court for two or more States or for two or more States and a Union territory." • Currently, India has three common High Courts: (i) Punjab & Haryana High Court (sitting at Chandigarh), (ii) Guwahati High Court serving Assam, Nagaland, Mizoram and Arunachal Pradesh, and (iii) the Common High Court for Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh (though now separate High Courts exist under new Acts). • The power is exclusively vested in the Parliament, not in the Supreme Court (Articles 124-147), the President (Article 52), or the Union Cabinet (Article 75). • Hence, only the Parliament can create or alter common High Courts through legislation. Question: Which one among the following motions cannot be made while introducing an ordinary Bill in the Parliament ?
Option_A: That the Bill be taken into consideration
Option_B: That the Bill be circulated for the purpose of eliciting public opinion
Option_C: That the Bill be referred to a Select Committee
Option_D: That the Bill be referred to a Joint committee of the House without the concurrence of the other House
Explanation: Solution: Concept: The introduction stage of an ordinary Bill allows certain preliminary motions; referring to a Joint Committee requires both Houses' concurrence, so motion D is invalid. Explanation: An ordinary Bill passes through three readings in each House. At the first reading, the Bill is introduced and its title is read. After introduction, the mover may propose motions for the Bill's further consideration. These motions include: that the Bill be taken into consideration (A), that it be circulated for public opinion (B), or that it be referred to a Select Committee (C). A motion to refer the Bill to a Joint Committee of the two Houses must be agreed to by both Houses separately. Without the concurrence of the other House, such a motion cannot be made in a single House. Therefore, motion D is not permissible at the introduction stage. Answer: Option D. That the Bill be referred to a Joint committee of the House without the concurrence of the other House © examsnet.com

Question: Which one among the following was eliminated by the 44th Amendment Act of the Parliament?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: The 44th Amendment Act of 1978 eliminated the Right to Property as a fundamental right, converting it into a mere legal right. Explanation: The 44th Amendment was enacted in 1978 by the Janata Party government. It repealed Article 19(1)(f) and Article 31 of the Constitution, which guaranteed the Right to Property as a fundamental right to every citizen. After this amendment, the Right to Property was removed from Part III (Fundamental Rights) and became a legal right under Article 300A. As a legal right, it could no longer be directly enforced in the Supreme Court under Article 32. Other fundamental rights were not affected by this amendment. The Right against Exploitation (Article 23) remains a fundamental right. The Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32) is still a fundamental right and cannot be suspended except as provided by the Constitution. The Right to Education was added as a fundamental right much later by the 86th Amendment Act of 2002. Thus, among the four options, only the Right to Property was eliminated from fundamental rights by the 44th Amendment. Answer: Right to Property © examsnet.com

Marble is a metamorphic rock formed from limestone under heat and pressure. Halite is a chemical sedimentary rock (rock salt) formed by evaporation of water. Question: Ozone layer, which absorbs the ultra-violet radiation, is found in which one of the following layers of the atmosphere?
Explanation: Solution: Concept: The ozone layer is a region of the atmosphere that absorbs harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation from the Sun. It is located in the stratosphere. Explanation: Earth's atmosphere is divided into layers based on temperature and composition. The lowest layer is the troposphere, extending from the ground up to about 10 km. Most weather and clouds occur here. Above the troposphere lies the stratosphere, which reaches from about 10 km to 50 km altitude. The ozone layer is found within the stratosphere. Ozone molecules in this layer absorb most of the Sun's high-energy UV radiation, protecting life on Earth. Commercial jets often fly in the lower stratosphere because it is less turbulent. Above the stratosphere is the mesosphere (50–85 km), where meteors burn up and temperatures are very low. Beyond that are the thermosphere and ionosphere (85–600 km+), where satellites orbit and auroras occur. The correct option from the given choices is the stratosphere. Answer: D.
